\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Mr. Santo Napoli stated welcome everyone and we are going to kick start this Public Hearing.  He stated today is Wednesday, June 6, 2026 and stated that we will start with a Roll Call, please.  He stated that so Allentown City Council tonight will take testimony and consider for possible adoption an ordinance defining and regulating Data Centers at a Public Hearing right now at 6:00 PM.  Copies of the full text of this ordinance and Reports of this legislation are available on the website.  Immediately following this Public Hearing, City Council may adopt this amendment to the Zoning Ordinance at the regularly scheduled City Council meeting right at 6:30 PM or whenever they finish with this.  To avoid any confusion, he would like to note that testimony tonight will be taken on this Ordinance before Council, Bill 20 and Bill 20 only.  The proposed Data Center Project at 2401 Emmaus Avenue is being considered at the Allentown Planning Commission meeting which takes place on Tuesday, June 9th at 12:15 PM right here in Council Chambers.  Residents will then be able to provide public comments regarding that particular project at that meeting with the Allentown Planning Commission.  The Emmaus Avenue Data Center is not a matter for City Council at this time.  Testimony tonight, will be focused on Bill 20.  All other comments can be shared at the City Council meeting after this, during Courtesy of the Floor, immediately following a Public Hearing.  He asked are we good?  He stated that so listen, if you are here to talk about 2401 Emmaus Avenue at this junction they are not taking testimony on that, but after this meeting, that is an opportunity for you to do so.  He stated that we are the same and this is a Public Hearing, we are following legal matters here.  He stated that all we are talking about is Bill 20, but after this meeting which will be around 6:30 - 6:45, they will have Courtesy of the Floor where any members of the public can discuss their concerns or feedback on 2401 Emmaus Avenue so that will happen immediately after this so that will be after this Public Hearing.   He stated that he is going to hand it off to Council's Solicitor, Ms Montero for the legal basis.\par
\par
Attorney Maria Montero stated that the purpose of this Hearing is for public commentary on Bill 20 as prescribed by the Pennsylvania Municipal Planning Code. She stated to Genesis Ortega, you can read the Bill.\par
\par
Ms. Genesis Ortega stated Bill 20 -Amends Part II General Legislation, Chapter 660 Zoning, Article 5 Uses, Table 660-4 Use Table and Section 660-38 Manufacturing & Industry Group, adding the use category Data Center Use; and Article 14 Measurements & Definitions, Section 660-135 Terms Beginning with "D" and Section 660-149 Terms Beginning with "R", adding the definition of Data Center, Data Center Accessory Use, and Renewable Energy.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated ok, thank you.  He stated that they are going to hand it off to the administration with our Planning Director and Managing Director, you have the floor.\par
\par
Mr. Frank Kane stated so what is on the table to be discussed this evening at this Hearing is that Bill 20, Bill 20 is an amendment to the city of Allentown's Zoning Code that creates a Data Center right now anyone wants to apply for a Data Center stating we don't have that .  That doesn't exist in our Code and did was to consider manufacturing use.  He stated so if you were to apply now and people have in the past have applied and it has just been a manufactured use so this creates some checks and balances and some provisions and creates extra oversight on proposed Data Centers.  It initiates and have to go through that additional level of Planning through Planning and Zoning and it puts some safeguards in.  If you put safeguards in and you vote for this amendment tonight, the next person that tries to undertake a Data Center in the city of Allentown will have to follow these Rules.  He stated if you don't vote for this tonight, Data Centers are still permitted, but they are just going to fall under manufacturing, general manufacturing.  He stated that is an overview and stated that he is going to turn it over to the city's Planning Director who is going to give a more in-depth explanation.\par
\par
Ms. Jennifer Gomez stated hey, good afternoon and thank you for the introduction.  She stated that her name is Jennifer Gomez and she is the Planning and Zoning Director for the city.  She stated that she would say just because she borrowed a slide here and also a Lehigh Valley Planning Commission and took one of the slides talking about Data Centers and it is their slide, not mine.  She stated it is their slide, not hers.  They said that every time, before any and they review all Data Centers that the Lehigh Valley on all Data Center ordinances and they always show this slide because it demonstrates or at least talks about the laws that work within and why we make the decisions and the regulations that we do.  All of the authority to regulate Zoning that has been given to us through the MPC Municipal Planning Code. All of the Land Development Regulations come through the MPC.  It gets very specific what the city can and can't regulate down to things like how many number of days they can take to review land development applications and in addition to the MPC, it is rooted in the US Constitution and also in Case Law which gives a lot of precedent, legal precedent in terms of how we handle these matters and what it comes down to for uses is the city cannot ban uses, we have to allow uses some where, but they also have a lot of control in terms of Planning for those uses and making them the choices that are right for our community.  She stated that is what they are trying to do here is to be proactive and with Bill 20 and crate some Data Center regulations and this new use that is emerging and evolving throughout the Lehigh Valley and throughout the country so if you can continue to the next slide, please.    She stated that this the Land Development process. She stated that there has been a lot of confusion she thinks in the media and on various websites as to what they are even hearing today.  She stated that they actually did get a Data Center proposed will come in at 2401 W Emmaus Avenue.  She stated that is being reviewed and it is being reviewed under the existing Zoning Ordinance.  She stated that doesn't mean the city doesn't have rules, it just means that they don't have Rules for Data Centers and so we still have all the city Codes.  We have the Health Codes.  We have the Public Safety Codes.  We have the Planning Codes, the Shade Tree Codes, Stormwater, Engineering, and Fire is important to this.  All of the Codes that they would review other projects and they have external review that happen on every single land development and that includes the Lehigh Valley Planning Commission.  The Allentown Environmental Advisory Council.  They send comments to LANTA,  to the School Board, Lehigh County Authority. She stated right now, they are going through that process with the one that's in.  She doesn't know if they have regulations.  She stated it is not that they don't have regulations.  They just have to just use the ones that we have in place of development.  She stated so there is a Planning Commission scheduled for it, June 9th.  She encouraged everyone just to stay on top of the website.  She stated that she is not sure and sometimes we might release the Staff Report.  They may or may not table based on some results.  She stated that is the process that we go through and a lot of people say how can I participate.  How do I get my voice heard for that particular meeting.  She stated that is the strongest way to have voice your voice heard to attend, but if you can't attend and they have a public comment email.  So it is public.comment@allentownpa.gov and please email them.  They are collecting all comments they received.  There are quite a few comments in the last couple of days, especially.  She stated to please keep sending those comments and they will compile everything and will all become part of the record that travels with this Plan.  She stated so that putting that aside for a minute and we want to talk about being proactive and how to get the best rules and regulations in place for the city and that is what they are looking at for Bill 20 and stated if she could look at the next slide.  She stated Bill 20, Data Center Ordinance.  She stated that she thinks again, perhaps maybe there is some perception and the vote here it to be more permissive and allow Data Centers by right.  That is absolutely not the case.  She stated that they are actually are trying to control this use and set minimum standards and regulations and additional reviews so we can evaluate to make sure that the infrastructure and all of the external location.  This at the first time, it says the Data Center Uses and finds it says what Zoning District it can go in.  She stated right now, it is the two most intense Zoning Industrial Zoning Designations.  They also have setbacks from property lines.  Giving specific separation for residential uses and other sensitive uses like churches and schools and daycares and they also have minimum lot size requirements for larger facilities and this is an important protection in Allentown because it says if you are going to do it, a large one of 50,000 square feet or more.  She stated that you really need to be on a really large lot within those industrial areas.  She stated that narrows the number of location where they can go substantially within Allentown.  Where there is a city largely of smaller lots and filled developments.  It really kinds of pushes them towards the Industrial areas and corridors. She stated that there are some areas you need to watch out for.  They are adjacencies to residentials, but we will continue to look and mitigate for that.  The Ordinance also sets forth landscaping and buffering standards.  If a Data Center is proposed, they want to make sure that they have extensive landscaping and screening to control both external appearance and also the impact such as noise.  She stated that they are going to require pre and post noise studies and also examining things like vibration and other environmental impacts far beyond whether they are in our Codes today.   She stated in addition the Code proposes water and sewage reporting.  She stated that they want to make sure that they know how much water and these are using and we have an appropriate amount of infrastructure in place to accommodate that and they are not taking more water than we can plan for energy demands.  She stated that we are asking for renewable energy.  She stated that they wanted to require renewable energy.  She stated that we are told, we can't legally do that based on the roles and limitations, but  they will work on it if there are any legal way that they can get in there.  They can continue to examine them because it would be ideal if they had some renewable energy production on site with these uses so we can continue to strive for that but we are told right now that is not legal.  Emergency response and fire safety planning, they will review and invoke fire lived use.  She stated our Fire Department has been very involved in review of the existing Data Center proposal that has come in.  They will look at electronic waste management and we also have design standards and aesthetics. Even with all these regulations which is heavily regulated and prescribed through this ordinance.  She stated that they realize that not all Data Centers are the same and they will need to do a case by case assessment of these Data Centers.  She stated so through that, they are not saying this Data Center is permitted use.  She stated if they go to the use table, they are not putting a P in permitted.  They are putting a special exception and what that Special Exception means is that there is a long process and thorough assessment that needs to go into that review and so what that looks like is first coming in and going through our planning office, it will go to the Environmental Advisory Committee which to date has not had a huge role with the use determination and they will evaluate all of the studies and then it will go to our Planning Commission to provide comments on the site before it goes to our Zoning Hearing Board and there will be a Public Hearing at the Zoning Hearing Board if all goes forward with this use. She stated that this is the general package and thinks they received a lot of feedback in terms of areas where additional standards are desired and they are.\par
\par
Audience members stated that they are getting feedback because they are broadcasting in the hallway so what you are hearing is the feedback.  She stated you have to close this door to eliminate the feedback.  If it gets warm, you can crack that door for some ventilation.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated ok.   He stated go ahead Ms. Gomez.  He stated hold on everyone.  Ms. Gomez has the floor right now.  Thank you. \par
\par
Ms. Jennifer Gomez stated that this is the starting point.  She stated right now, the city doesn't have the standards for Data Centers.  She stated that we want to add them and we can do this as a starting point and heard a lot of suggestions in the last couple of days in particular of ways that the ordinance can to be strengthened or proved or add additional standards and for that she will say that we are open to those discussions.  She stated that they don't want it to be the end of the discussion.  It can be the beginning of the discussion, but we do want to protect the city and they do want to get some rules in place to do that.  She just want to make sure that everyone keeps that in mind that they do want to give the city's protections which is why they are here.  She stated that if they can go to the next slide.  She stated that this has taken them a long time to get to where they are.  She stated that she thinks Data Centers are an emerging use.  They are changing.  They are evolving and they really starting hitting the Lehigh Valley last year.  She stated late last year and stated that she thinks it would get more media attention with that so when that started happening they said ok, here is this new use stating we need to regulate this use and we need to look into it.  She stated that it is not an easy process to adopt the Zoning Code.    It is a long process with a lot of reviews.  She stated that they started in winter of this year and they coordinated with the Environmental Advisory Committee and we said we need your help, please help us make this ordinance in a way that it is defensive and protects the environment.  She stated that they then took all of that to City Council so that was in January and in March they went to City Council and City Council introduced the ordinance then they went to Lehigh Valley Planning Commission Comprehensive Planning meeting in April and then they went to the Lehigh Valley Planning Commission full commission, also then they went to the Allentown Planning Commission, also in April and they went to the Allentown Economic Development Committee meeting on May 14 so this was she thinks six public meetings that they attended to discuss this use and all in preparation for this Public Hearing.  She stated that it took them all of these meetings to get to where they are today and have something to show you guys and this is a really important date for us because on May 17th, they advertised this Bill and this gave the city the advertising of this Bill and gave the city a lot of legal protections because now we have all of these standards that they can fall back on.  She stated that she thinks they will continue to work on it. They will continue to approve it and they are open to feedback and comments.  She stated that it concludes her comments.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated alright, welcome everyone and we are going to kick start this Public Hearing.  He stated today is Wednesday, June 6th and stated that we will start with a Roll Call.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated ok, thank you Ms Gomez.  He stated so this is a Public Hearing so he is going to open it up to the public.  He stated a reminder this is testimony on Bill 20.  He stated that everything they just saw on Bill 20, you are welcome to comment.  He stated that if they are any other comments you have regarding other Data Center issues or locations, save those for our next meetings right after this one.   He stated so Courtesy of the Floor, go ahead.  He asked the audience member to hold on.  He asked if someone can prop open the back door.  Just to get some fresh air, please.  He stated alright, thank you.  He stated go ahead.\par
\par
Mr. Kyle Ropsky, chair of the Environmental Advisory Council, stating that they are a volunteer board with the purpose to advise with non-binding recommendations on matters related to environmental protections and sustainability here in the city of Allentown.  He wanted to begin tonight by thanking everyone in this room.  He stated the city staff, elected officials, and most importantly, the Allentown residents and taxpayers that have shown up here tonight.  In the street, our city has always brought risk to our natural environment in various forms of pollution. The burdens of this pollution have often been disproportionately distributed onto our most vulnerable populations.  He stated that it is not right and it needs to change and we need to move toward a more equitable and healthy Allentown that works for all of us, not just some.   The EAP has sent over 40 review letters that included detail recommendations for the Bill and ultimately a letter of support that should be included on the agenda.  He stated that you all know this is not his first time at the podium discussing the importance of our environments and our natural resources with the value they bring to our community.  He stated that on many occasions, this room is not as populated as it should be, but tonight, it is and that means something.  He stated that he wants to maintain decorum, but can he please have a show of hands from the residents is the room who cares about protecting our environments from Data Centers.  He stated please, he would raise his second hand if it wasn't holding the microphone.  He stated that the people here care about our city.  They care about our air quality and our elders who suffer with respiratory issues.  They care about our water quality and our children who cannot safely and too often our water waze on a hot summer day.  They care about the future of our city and that is exactly why he is urging their support for the passaging of Bill 20.  He stated that this Bill is of discussion were transparent, collaborative and diligent work with the intent to protect our residents and our environment.  He stated that they are extremely grateful and blessed here at the city to have such an amazing team in our city staff.   they have worked tirelessly over the course of several months to develop a wording in this amendment. He stated that they engaged the EAC early on in the process and ensured the final language includes a review of a proposed Data Center develop by the EAC giving the public critical access to these plans ahead of time.  On a Monday night meeting, they saw a record number of attendees and they hope this engagement continues in the future for future proposals could inevitable come up for review.  The EAC is encouraged to see strong core requirements for environmental review, infrastructure water capacity analysis, energy planning, noise evaluation and heat mitigation and site buffering.  These studies help identify and address potential impacts early, protecting our residents, our environmental resources and our taxpayer dollars.  He stated importantly, a specific requirement for any proposal will be determined to be reviewed by the city, the Planning Commission and the AEC allowing standards and mitigation measures to be tailored involving technologies and unique conditions of each site over time.   He stated that he cannot stress enough the importance of the passage of this Bill for the sake of our environments or our residents.  He thanked them for their time here tonight and strongly urged them to bring this monumental effort to the finish line for the protection of our city and our community.  Thank you.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated your name for the record, please.\par
\par
Ms. Ginny Marcelle Kerslake stated that she is with an organization and asked does she get five minutes.  She stated that she does not know if she will use all the five minutes.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated five, yeah.\par
\par
Ms. Ginny Marcelle Kerslake stated her name is Ginny Marcelle Kerslake and asked does she need to spell that.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated that's ok.\par
\par
Ms. Ginny Marcelle Kerslake stated that she is a resident of Pennsylvania.  She is the Senior Organizer of Food and Water Watch, Pennsylvania.  She stated that she will start by saying over the past year, she has been constantly across the state, mostly in Central and Eastern Pennsylvania, helping municipalities pass protective ordinances for this new use.  Just like you are aiming to do right now.  She stated that she commend them for that.  She stated unfortunately she would like to say that this ordinance that you have before you.  This Data Center ordinance is unfortunately one of the worse ones she has seen and you just heard the gentleman say that there were a record number of people on the meeting last night with the EAC.  She attended part of that meeting and people were in opposition with this and had grave concerns about it.  She stated that she is going to raise three key ones for you.  First of all, this ordinance allows this high impact industrial use in both the IM and the IG District.  She stated that you do not have to do that.  You do not have to open up both of those districts for this and again, this is a high impact industrial use.  It is not compatible with the description of the industrial general zone.  She stated that this should be restricted to the industrial manufacturing zone.  She stated secondly, this 200 foot setback from homes and other sensitive receptors is grossly insufficient.  She stated that it is well documented that the emissions of the high skilled Data Centers extends even from miles from the source and as a result, setbacks in Pennsylvania that they are seeing now from other municipalities are on the order of thousands of feet from sensitive receptors, like homes.  She stated that she can name a bunch of them, but maybe the ones that means the most to you are the most recent guidelines released by Chester County and Montgomery County Planning Commission that advised that Data Centers shall be a minimum of one thousand feet from residential uses, residential districts and/or other sensitive receptors.  She read in some minutes that an ordinance from Penn Future had been used to craft this and stated maybe that's where the 200 feet came from.  The only place that she has seen that is from industry ordinances that they have presented.  She wants them to know that Penn Future has recently had retracted that 200 feet.  She stated ok, so that is no longer recommended even by Penn Future.  She stated thirdly, there are no decommissioning requirements in this model ordinance and this Data Center ordinance and that would include financial security.  There is a very real risk because this technology is advancing that these huge energy and water consuming facilities will no longer be needed and viable and so they will walk away.  She stated in five to 10 years this industry is even saying that.  You need your community with these stranded assets and also the costs.  You either have that blight or you will have the cost of cleaning this site up, if you haven't required that financial security and that will fall on all the taxpayers and it will be a lot of money.  She stated she sees she just have one minute left and want to address one thing that we heard from she thinks the Planning Director.  It was stated that if a Data Center ordinance came into them right now, it could go anywhere and would fall under manufacturing uses.   She stated that she thoroughly read your Zoning Ordinance.  Data Centers are not a specified use under your manufacturing and there was no savings clause for any use that is not specified.  She stated so your ordinance truly is substantially invalid for Data Centers and what actually would happen is if somebody wants to build one, they would have to you with a Landowner Curative Amendment and go through that process so that is where you are at.  This is not an easy task if you don't vote for this.  She stated what she is recommending is you deny this insufficient Data Center Ordinance and instead pass a resolution tonight to enact a municipal Curative Amendment which is actually in accordance with your own Zoning Ordinance when there is an invalidity and give yourselves an 180 day pause on all those Landowner Curative Amendments and applications for a really good ordinance to be passed. This is your chance to do that and stated that she hopes Council takes it.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated pause for one second.  he stated everyone, he wants to make clear what the expectations are tonight.  Everyone has a right to speak.  Everyone has a right to give us our feedback.  He stated that he just wants to be respectful to anyone who has the floor.  Whether it is one of his colleagues.  Whether it is the administration.  Whether it is you, members of the public who we all want to hear from.  He stated that there should not be interruptions whether you are in favor of what they are saying or whether you are not in favor.  He stated that they just need to be respectful.  When someone has the floor, let's give them the floor.  Everyone will have an opportunity and we will get through this.  He stated that they are here for it and they want to hear it, but he just want it to be professional and respectful.  He will apply these Rules evenly to everyone in the room so that includes Council.  That includes the administration.  He stated that they are not going to talk over anyone and they are not going to cheer when they like something or   geer when they don't like something.  He stated everyone gets a floor so thank you, everyone.   He stated go ahead.\par
\par
Mr. Spencer Snig stated that he is a local businessman and work with AI and technology all the time and know that it is bad for economy and it is bad for the environment. He stated as the previous speaker just said remediation and if they do have to clear out all those servers, there are a lot of heavy metals and toxic stuff so it could not be good.  The question is how do you word things in your bills so that it is defensible in court.  He stated one of the biggest things and the easiest way to defend it is economic impact studies.  If they can prove to have a positive impact on Allentown, that is a thing, but in fact most AI technologies actually have a negative impact on the environment and also business.  He stated that if you look at and stated that another thing he talked about was you got to worry about and stated that it was taking over a storage facility and with a storage facility you have people that are moving boxes and all that and a Data Center you don't.  Basically, you have a couple security guards and breaks and changes any data and you also have a technician come in once in a blue moon and asked how many times you have physically taken your computer somewhere to be repaired.  It doesn't really happen that often so that means it is not going to be supplying a lot of jobs.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated one moment, please.  He stated that this is only for Bill 20 so as long as your comments are towards Bill 20. \par
\par
Mr. Spencer Snig stated that he is just using it as an example.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated again, if you have more, he would be happy to hear it at the next portion at our next meeting.  He stated that this is only for Bill 20.\par
\par
Mr. Spencer Snig stated and also for Bill 20, economic variety so one of the problems that you are going to have are people are saying I want to build many Data Centers. If they fall below your requirements so if you say we have to have economic variety then you can reject a bid for a smaller server.  \par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated ok.  He stated thank you and if you have more, you are welcome to stay for the next portion of courtesy of the floor.  \par
\par
Mr. Spencer Snig stated thank you.\par
\par
Mr. Lewis Shupe, 11201 Hamilton - Allentown, PA stated hello there.  Can you hear?  Good you can hear me.  He stated his name is Lewis Shupe and stated hello.  He stated that he is a Facebook Group Administrator in the Allentown, PA community.  The largest group of its kind in Allentown.  He stated 35,000 members.  Generally vetted and organized for civil discourse.  He stated that he is also a retired web master/programmer.  He stated that he has been working with AI a lot in the past couple of years and stated that it scares the living she*t out of him, ok and stated that he is serious.  He stated as far as Bill 20 goes, forget about Bill 20.  Ban it outright at least for 180 days until more information comes in because the chatter he is seeing right now, these Data Centers that are being proposed and include technology which he has been studying for a long time.  He stated that they are going to be using these Data Centers for mass surveillance and when that happens, it is going to be a lot harder to take them off.  He stated ban them outright.  Thank you.\par
\par
Mr. Nick Nicholoff, stated hello and stated that his name is Nick Nicholoff.  He stated that he lives on the southside and a current member of the Allentown School District's board of directors and work professionally in Policy and Organizational Development.  He stated that today he is here before Council as an individual to express concerns and a lack of definitions of AI Data Centers and specific.  Touch on their impact and briefly comment on your Bill.  He stated that he would like to highlight in particular an aspect of AI Data Centers with repercussions that may be more intense for Allentown and the Lehigh Valley which is their contribution to particular matter of air pollution.  A study led by Harvard Researcher Dr. Michael Cork reviewed Data Centers and Loudoun County Virginia which is an area similar in size and population to our own, totaling to about 800,000 square feet and found that the PM pollution alone would contribute up to $100 million of additional health damages and 6.5 premature deaths on the region per year.  The cost of that is born by the citizens of the area, not the owners of the Centers themselves.  If put in use as an AI Data Center, the currently proposed 244,000 square foot facility on Emmaus Avenue would contribute 1.5 tons of PM per year under their optimum operating circumstances, but they will likely see an EPA permit for 70 tons of emissions per year.  He stated for context, that is the equivalent 6,300 trucks worth of pollution, operating 100,000 miles each within the area of the Lehigh Valley.  The Lehigh Valley is a basin with this historically poor air quality record.  It is the 50th most polluted air quality metro area in the country and it is the third highest (inaudible).  If we were to face similar air quality impacts in Louden or in our region with its already poor air quality record and threaten to make our situation of residents untenable or displace or possibly contribute to the premature deaths of many residents.  With that said he believes their amendment is a necessity, even if it is room for improvement.  He encouraged Council to pass it.  It is relatively well written and it takes important first steps to address Data Centers.  It would be better to pass this now, and make amendments in the future then to let things stand as is and have more Data Centers sneak through on technicalities.  He stated though he would encourage them to add language to differentiate between standard commercial Data Centers and AI Data Centers.  The later in which he would highly encourage be classified as heavy industrial so that they will have more oversight and it would preclude them from being present in residential and commercial areas such as a nonprofit dedicated to helping children with medical complexities which will certainly be exacerbated by having a mass pollutant right across the street from them.  Thank you.\par
\par
}
agenda_items.title:
Bill 20
Amending Part II General Legislation, Chapter 660 Zoning, Article 5 Uses, Table 660-4 Use Table and Section 660-38 Manufacturing & Industry Group, adding the use category Data Center Use; and Article 14 Measurements & Definitions, Section 660-135 Terms Beginning with “D” and Section 660-149 Terms Beginning with “R”, adding the definition of Data Center, Data Center Accessory Use, and Renewable Energy.

NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING

Notice is hereby given that the Allentown City Council will consider for possible adoption an Ordinance Amending Part II General Legislation, Chapter 660 Zoning, Article 5 Uses, Table 660-4 Use Table and Section 660-38 Manufacturing & Industry Group, adding the use category Data Center Use; and Article 14 Measurements & Definitions, Section 660-135 Terms Beginning with “D” and Section 660-149 Terms Beginning with “R”, adding the definition of Data Center, Data Center Accessory Use, and Renewable Energy. 

City Council will take public testimony and consider the foregoing at a Public Hearing on Wednesday, June 3, 2026 at 6:00 PM in Council Chambers, 435 Hamilton Street, Allentown, PA 18101. Copies of the full text of this Ordinance are available to any interested party for examination and copying at the City Clerk’s Office or for inspection during regular business hours at the offices of this newspaper and the Lehigh County Department of Law. All documents can also be found on the City website. City Council may adopt this amendment to the Zoning Ordinance at the regularly scheduled City Council Meeting at 6:30 PM on June 3, 2026 immediately following this Public Hearing.

\par
Mr. Lester Wagner a resident at 2432 28th Street SW.  He has been a homeowner for over 40 years.  He is within a half mile of the subject proposed center.  He stated that he just wants to comment in general.  Data Center investment and expansion is taking place at unreasonably speculative rates.  This unbridaled advancement is neither productive, prudent or has proven advantageous to the public in general.  The AI load of such centers is expected to expand 50 percent by 2030.  Now being about 25 percent.  The energy burden for AI is 10 times that of ordinary data.  The plain truth about AI is that it is highly empowering, not only for good, but for fraud and public abuse.  There is no legislation to effectively sort this issue out much less speak to legal regulations over the resources which it uses in access.  It is energy, utility, water, and other issues. Not to mention noise abatement and other things.  He stated further, the public distribution benefit of these Data Centers is surely not uniform.  He stated for this reason, any investors should probably bare the full cost burden of operation.  This should include full responsibility for total energy use of being the cost of remote or local generation as well as full cost to build and maintain the required distribution to man infrastructure.   This is something that PPL should have address and tell us about the factual information. Other local utility mans for water and cooling must be similarly born by the investors such the public is not mandated to bare our share of the highly speculative operational cost having unknown positive and/or destructive for fraudulent purpose (inaudible) and businesses who employed Data Center Services should bare the full fair market value of the service provided.  Thank you.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated thank you.\par
\par
Mr. Adam Bond stated that he would like to continue his remarks from before.  He thought he would have a little more time.  He stated in summary, he would say that we always look at these things from a Specialist view.  They look at them from a project by project view.   They don't take into an account the cumulative effect  that not just Data Center development, but all of this development entails in this region has had and now they are being asked to contemplate an entire early new category development who demands may dwarf even the warehouse.  Data Centers do not merely occupy the land.  They consume an enormous quantities of electricity and substantial quantities of water and their viability depends upon infrastructure whose costs often extend far beyond the boundaries of any individual project.  One of the least understood aspects of our electric system is that markets begin pricing a future demands years before facilities are even constructed.  Capacity auctions determine the cost of insuring adequate electric generation several years in advance.  He stated that this month for instance, electrical suppliers will buy capacity for 2027 and 2028. Utilities and grid operators do not simply respond to existing demands.  They respond to projected demand.  When developers propose massive data centers, the electricity system begins planning for the possibilities that those facilities will come online.  Generation capacity must be reserved.  Transmission upgrades must be considered.  Infrastructure investments must be evaluated.  The result is that ratepayers can end up paying the cost for the preparing for demand that may not ever actually arrive.  The public assumes the risks while private investors pursue the opportunity.  These pressures are compounded by a second reality that deserves far more attention.  He stated that decades of deferred infrastructure investment.  He stated for many years utilities operated under a logic that was short-term, but it is a disaster in the long-term categorized by a model repeated in conference rooms and cubicles in PPL Tower throughout the 1980s, 90s and 2000s. The bill of deferral inevitably becomes due and when it does, it is far larger than it would have been had the work has been done incrementally over time.  He stated today we face combined consequences of those deferred investments and an unprecedented proposed electrical demand.   \par

Courtesy of the Floor
Please observe the Rules of Council when given privilege of the floor. A copy of the Council Rules can be found on the council agenda on the website. If you would like to speak, we are asking that you fill out a card – they are on the back table provide them to the clerk before speaking. Include your name and address. When speakers have the privilege of the floor, personal insults, attacks, name calling or other behavior that is inconsistent with the purpose of conducting official business will not be tolerated.

Courtesy of the Floor is meant to provide public comments on items that are not on the agenda. Public comment during consideration of ordinances, resolutions and motions are limited by topic – your comments must be relevant to the subject matter of the proposed legislation. Public comments are taken before 	council votes on legislation. 

You are given the privilege of the floor to provide public comment; it is not a question and answer session. State your position clearly and concisely for consideration. If you speak on behalf of yourself, you have three minutes and if you are speaking on behalf of a group that has several members present, you will be given five minutes in place of everyone coming to the podium. Please address the Council President not individual councilpersons or city staff. Refrain from insulting or defaming staff, officials, and the public; refrain from using offensive language, cursing, and making noises while other people are speaking. Please be aware that comments and/or behavior in violation of these rules will result in a forfeiture of all remaining time and you will be asked to return to your seat.

Ms. Ce Ce Gerlach stated president Santo she would like to make a Motion and before doing so as someone who has been in the audience where you are there all night and then you are asked to come back and stated that she appreciates those who have bills to pay, jobs to work, babysitters to find, gas to put in the car, and unfortunately for you, this Motion will if you care about this require for you to come back if it passes.  She stated so because there is not exactly what the legal clarity and the Council President has asked the City Council Solicitor to perform an LSR and an LSR is a legal review to see what they can and can't do.  She stated because of that she doesn't think that they are in a place to vote for or against this ordinance right now.  She stated that she will make a Motion to table Bill 20 until the next Council meeting which is June 17th to give the City Council Solicitor time to complete an LSR.\par
\par
Mr. Jeremy Binder stated that he will Second it.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated ok so we have a Motion on the floor.  Ms. Gerlach made a Motion to Table until June 17th and Councilperson Binder is a Second.\par
\par
Mr. Michael Hanlon stated that Candida had to leave so you have her back on the line.  He stated that it is a Motion to Table the Bill until the June 17th Council meeting.  \par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated ok so can we call a vote on the Motion.\par
\par
Ms. Genesis Ortega stated that she has 7 yays and no nays on the Motion.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated before he forgets and is going to need some help from and stated that they still have another Motion.  It is lingering that vice president Mota made and seconded by Affa.    \par
\par
Attorney Marie Montero stated that they can ask Councilwomen Mota if she would like to withdraw her Motion at this point.\par
\par
Dr. Cynthia Mota stated that she would like to withdraw her Motion at this point.  \par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated ok, he just wants to make sure it was out there and did not want anyone to forget about it.\par
\par
Audience member asked for clarification on the LSR and asked if it is for some background on the.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated after the meeting.  He stated after the meeting you can come up and we can help you with that.  \par
\par
Audience member stated that she will be heading back because she has a two hour drive.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated so very quickly and asked if it is four Councilpersons, Mr. Hanlon.\par
\par
Mr. Michael Hanlon stated yes.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated four Councilpersons will have to sign on and that will enable our Solicitor to do an LSR.  He stated that they will give the questions of their concerns and then she will do the research and Council will get back to us in a timely manner.  \par
\par
Audience member asked about a Municipal Curative Amendment.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated yep.  It is obviously one of the big ones so that is a Plan.\par
\par
Audience member stated yep, thanks.  \par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated so as it was mentioned in the Motion that will come back to Council for June 17th so mark your calendars.  He stated that they will move along and next on the Agenda is our Consent Agenda.  He stated that they have one item on the Consent Agenda stating he believes R69.\par

agenda_items.title:
Bill 20
Amending Part II General Legislation, Chapter 660 Zoning, Article 5 Uses, Table 660-4 Use Table and Section 660-38 Manufacturing & Industry Group, adding the use category Data Center Use; and Article 14 Measurements & Definitions, Section 660-135 Terms Beginning with “D” and Section 660-149 Terms Beginning with “R”, adding the definition of Data Center, Data Center Accessory Use, and Renewable Energy.

Bill 45
Amends Chapter 19, Civil Service Board, of the Codified Ordinances, titled “Rules of the City of Allentown Civil Service Board Governing the Appointment and Promotion of Police Officers and Firefighters” by removing “Failed to register with the Selective Service System” as a disqualifier for the Civil Service Test. 

The proposed Bill approves the City of Allentown Police and Fire Civil Service Board’s repeal of its Rules that automatically disqualify an applicant for police officer or firefighter from examination for or selection from an eligibility list if the applicant has failed to register with the Selective Service System. The Bill modernizes the Board’s Rules and harmonizes the Rules with both Pennsylvania law and recently enacted Federal law

R70
Appoints a Temporary Deputy Controller for the City of Allentown.until that time when the City of Allentown City Council appoints an interim City Controller.

Bill 48
Amending the 2026 Trexler Fund by authorizing a supplemental appropriation in the amount of Three Hundred Twenty-Two Thousand Nine Hundred Fifty-Five Dollars and Fifty Cents ($322,955.50) to the Parks and Recreation Department to support the operating and capital budgets. This is inclusive of the City Match required in the agreement which needs to correspondingly increase Eighteen Thousand Two Hundred Eighty Dollars and Fifty Cents. ($18,280.50) to follow the 6% match requirement. This is part of the 2026 Trexler Capital Project allocation.

Bill 20
Amending Part II General Legislation, Chapter 660 Zoning, Article 5 Uses, Table 660-4 Use Table and Section 660-38 Manufacturing & Industry Group, adding the use category Data Center Use; and Article 14 Measurements & Definitions, Section 660-135 Terms Beginning with “D” and Section 660-149 Terms Beginning with “R”, adding the definition of Data Center, Data Center Accessory Use, and Renewable Energy.

Mr. Santo Napoli stated that Mr. Ritter, you are up and state welcome.\par

Mr. Keith Ritter stated thank you.  He stated so he and his sister and a couple other folks and stated that he just moved back to Pennsylvania, Allentown stating he was gone for many years and since he has been back about a year, he has been staying with his sister half of the time, during the winter and stay up at a cottage close by often on Emmaus Avenue. The point is they are kind of hoping that something could be done for that area because it's, the noise and the motorcycles, the loud is horrendous. He stated that he means it is bad and the speeding.  If anybody was working on the street and would have been right there, they would have murdered.  They would have been killed and he thinks there were things done before and like he said he has been gone for a long time so he is just speaking because his car is gone.  He had to go and buy another car, but this happened just the other night.  Again, they may want to say something too if it is possible and they don't know who else to do or to say or who to talk to.    \par

Mr. Santo Napoli stated ok, they have your information and if there are some department heads or folks, they might get back to you with some updates. Maybe there are some Plans stated that he can't speak to that at this moment, but they have his information.  He asked do we have your phone number and email.  \par

Mr. Keith Ritter stated that phone number and address, yes.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated to Mr. Ritter, leave your email too.  He stated that will be helpful. \par

Mr. Keith Ritter asked could he give it to them.\par

Mr. Santo Napoli stated to include your email stating he appreciates it.  He stated that he will see if anyone has any updates regarding that situation.  Thank you.  He asked is it any other Courtesy of the Floor on non Agenda items.  He asked do you want to speak.  Go ahead and asked the name for the record, please.\par
\par
Mr. David Bortz stated that he doesn't know if there is a board or committee or anything like that, but he knows William Allen High School they used to have a William Allen High School Construction Company.  He stated there is a club that they organize and they partner with Alvin H. Butz and they designed the 17th Street, right there on 17th Street and stated that he thinks it is Turner.  He stated that digital sign there they done that and partnered with Alvin H. Butz for that and what he wanted to do for a class gift even for the (inaudible) programs.  He stated that he has been trying to organize it, but sometimes it just falls when it gets past person to person to person and nothing really happens.  He stated that he was wondering if somebody or some organization can help organize it.  He stated that he had a mold of a reading bench that he wanted to donate for their graduating class to another class of William Allen High School. They already have a mold and design of it, but they don't have it actually built yet.  It can be shipped and the cost of  those is probably about 3,000 and he just wanted to see how would they be able to go about implementing that.  He talked to the Allentown School District or the Council people or however it goes.  He stated that if he could get any assistance or help because it would be a great idea for providing something like that for William Allen High School for having a nice reading bench outside. You will have some beautiful trees and architecture and everything else.  He stated maybe a brand new paint job will be nice too for that high school, especially after going to the states.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated that he is going to defer because there is one of his colleagues that can totally take of this and with Mr. Pungo next to him and he thinks Mr. Pungo can give some of his thoughts.  He suggested that Mr. Bortz leave his information and you guys can continue the conversation at a later day.  \par
\par
Mr. Cristian Pungo stated that he was going to say this is not a typical City Council thing, but you struck some luck because he actually still help with the construction company at William Allen still going strong so if Mr. Bortz leaves his info stating that he would love to connect to see if they can get them in touch with the Principal Nosh over at William Allen and just going through the next steps here and thinks it is a great things and they always appreciate people who want to help and continue to give back to the schools so he will also have Genesis if she doesn't mind sharing and stated that he doesn't know if they are sticking around, but sharing his contact info with him stating you can also have that.\par
\par
Mr. David Bortz stated that future generations definitely appreciate that as well. \par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated thank you.   It is great on your part.  \par
\par
Mr. Michael Staller asked could he actually follow up on a couple of things to jog his memory.  \par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated sure.  Come on up and we will wrap up courtesy of the floor.     \par
\par
Mr. Michael Staller stated that he used to stay at the Allentown Rescue Mission at 355 Hamilton and it is great that it is only men.  He stated only he thinks at some point having a female only place which he knows there is other things like that, but specifically for females as well.  He stated that he gets nervous during public speaking.  He stated that is one or two kind of based off of what you were talking about.  He stated about the ATC for the LANTA, you got the digital screens, right and it makes it pretty easy to figure out where you are going and what direction.  At the BTC, in Bethlehem they know it is not a lot of space there, but you do have the car garage, the garage.  He stated he doesn't know.  It would be nice to put digital screens at that one because at least for him, he could clearly see where they need to go without asking over and over again.  He is relying on people who may or may not have your best interest in mind.  It is a cool thing.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated quickly, remind me your name for the record.\par
\par
Mr. Michael Staller stated his name.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated that secondly you stated to Bethlehem Transit Center.\par
\par
Mr. Michael Staller stated yes.  He said that you have the screens of the ATC here so the BTC stating that he uses them all.  He stated that the BTC have, but you don't have the actual and physical with the typing.  The digital screens give you more info to figure it out.  The timing of when they are and stated sorry.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated that he is happy to hear that.  He stated that they do not have any control of Bethlehem's facility.  You have to reach out to Bethlehem's City Council, but that is something that you can reference. \par
\par
Mr. Michael Staller stated that he is sorry and apologized.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated that you can tell them hey, I saw this is Allentown and you would love to see it over there.  Unfortunately, we don't have any control over it.  \par
\par
Mr. Michael Staller stated that he appreciates it.  Thanks.  \par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated thanks for mentioning that.  He stated that they appreciate it and going to keep the meeting moving.  He stated we are going to get started with our first agenda item which is a presentation on Bill 46.  He stated Ms. Ortega, go ahead.\par
\par
Ms. Genesis Ortega read Bill 46.  \par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli thanked Ms. Ortega and stated that he will pass it off to the administration.  Take it away, Mr. Kane.  \par
\par
Mr. Frank Kane stated first he would like to take a moment and mention that how it is related to the Bill.  He stated that we want to recognize the victims of the tragic gun violence over this weekend.  He stated that he wants to let them know that they are going to be hosting a, the mayor is going to be hosting tomorrow, the District Attorney and a few members of Counsel and community leaders to talk about our strategic plan that we put together on violence so he would like to mention that if he can.  He stated moving on, they are here tonight to present on the DROP Pension Plan.  He stated that he has with him and stated that he thinks they know Chief Roca of the Allentown Police Department.  He stated Sergeant Chris Matthews who is the President of the FOP and we have stating Bina could not be with us so we have Finance people here from her office too who can talk about the numbers.  He stated that he thinks they already know that the DROP Pension is an opportunity for us to retain some of the top leadership of the department.  There are officers who have been here for 20 years who can stay and help, mentor and train other younger newer officers.  he stated that we bring them in and can avoid and have a number of officers eligible for retirement. We can avoid a mass retirement if we provide this benefit.  He stated that it is best that the Chief did a good job explaining this in the information section the other day. He happened to turn it over to Chief Roca who is pretty good at the details.\par
\par
Chief Charles Roca stated thank you and good evening Council.  He stated that one of the things that he wants to make clear first and foremost is that this is not about a money grab.  This is about making sense with public safety and part of that is investment in the officers.  He stated for many years, Allentown has built its representation on public safety, public works, public health and in this capacity with our officers, the DROP Pension is something that establishes as a retention tool. It doesn't have a brain drain.   He stated that they are talking about years of experience and he has lived through it.  When they have 160 something officers and it really impacted public safety.  Crimes started to creep up, where they weren't able to answer calls as quickly and the issues were coming out of hand.  They had built through hard work and dedication of many officers over time and along with our partners and community, a safe environment. Is there work to be done, absolutely.   There is work to be done.  He stated that with this drop, what it will do, it will allow officers to maintain their positions, move forward in a positive way and add years of service to the police department.  Currently, as it stands, we are looking at about a potential 40 officers that can retire at the end of this year.  That would bring us down to that 165 number. This is not a threat.  It is not on anything that is surprising.  Policing takes investment.  Public Safety is something that is very valuable and many of these officers have worked decades in the department and it is important that we keep them.  He stated having said that, it is also about from administrative standpoint that they are working to replenish the body and make sure that we hit our authorized strength.  Recruitment is very difficult in this day and age and many departments are fighting over the same pool of candidates. It is really a market for an individual wanting to become an Allentown Police Officer.  What makes a city attractive to an officer or a potential officer.  He stated that they get involved in the actual of fighting a crime, of conducting an investigation, of building a relationship with their community, specializing in different things that we have in our department and becoming and building those relationships to the point where it's not just a job, it becomes a passion, it becomes a career and he will tell them last year they had 14 retirements which is a little bit above the number of what they normally have.  Had they had the Pension back then, that number would have probably only had been four officers that would have retired.  He stated that is not to say that we had a drop in service, but we have a drop individuals that were being productive in their assignments which had led to massive reductions in crime.  Individuals that have a passion for law enforcement, for getting feedback from the community and this at no end is an easy job.  It is something where it takes commitment by the people that decide to wear the uniform.  It is very, very easy to go after police officer and say that you are not doing your job, but he invites folks to take the test, become part of the Allentown Police Force and establish a legacy of compassion and change that we want to bring here to this city and having said that with this being a retention tool, it is important that they also contain and recruit and having this available will be a good recruitment tool for individuals considering where they want to go and where they want to put a career in.  What he is notices in trends in employment is that individuals who work in a location for three or four years can belong to something else.  What they want to have as individuals that are career minded that want to serve a city for 20 plus years.  That want to be able to more forward.  If you are not aware, the city of Allentown currently has two different pension systems.  He stated one where you have those who were hired before 2009 that goes up to 70 percent in 25 years and those who were hired after 2009 who are limited and restricted to twenty years at 50 percent so the incentive to stay and cultivate leaders and a succession plan becomes more difficult if there is not an incentive to stay when you are talking about investments and what's important, if they go down to 160 officers, it will result in massive amounts of mandatory overtime.  He stated that they can't afford that here in the summer coming up. He stated that they realized some incidents of violence which are very very bad for our community, but are not going to sit back and do nothing about it.  He stated that their officers are invested in making sure that we solve crimes, that we hold people accountable, that that person who decides to squeeze a trigger with a gun and causes a homicide is brought to justice.  The same pain that a community feels reverberates through the department as well.  We do not want to see tragedies on the streets.  We have to make sure that the investment in public safety is real and that is why he is coming to them and implore them to consider this and make sure that it is implemented.  His position is that if it is fiscally sound and follow through with a transparent process, it is going to be a benefit to the city and as we work to improve our position within the city and address the quality of life crimes.  They have many different plans and situations that we are implementing and our work with our partners to improve that quality of life, but it takes the most important asset and he sit here to them and became Chief in June of '21 and verified as full Chief in September that same year.  He stated that it has been five years since he has been Chief.  He stated within that swearing in and that confirmation process, he talked about his Plan of changing Allentown.  It has bore fruit.  He stated that they had improved technology and improved relationships with our community.  Not everybody is going to agree with policing if that is ok.  He stated that they still will be there to serve that person in that community and in that neighborhood.  He stated that he wants to let them know that they are on point today is about talking about the DROP and what it's about and for him, he looks at it as an investment in maintaining, the good officers that they have that want to continue providing Allentown and not to consider going to second career, but rather they can look at having the DROP Pension and in addition to the Pension which will help them financially.  He stated that they talk about Wellness Initiatives.  It is not only about resilience and mental health and those things that officers experience a high level of trauma for the various calls of service that they are on and in part of this is to make sure that they are taking care of.  That our officers have worked for 20 plus years and have something that they can value.  An investment into our community, in showing and telling our officers that we value them and there are no cost that he could think of that can fit that, but these are all steps in the right direction.  He stated that he would like to invite Sergeant Chris Matthews from the FOP to kind of speak on that.  He wanted them to speak together because technically on the administration, the police administration, he represents the body, which is our Police Union.  He stated that he thinks they marched together in this in saying we want what is best for the officers which in turn will be valuable for our community.\par
\par
Sergeant Chris Matthews stated thank you Chief.  He stated at first he would like to start off by saying thank you to the administration for bringing this benefit of the FOP and working with us to kind of work out through all the finite details of it.  It is kind of follow up on what Chief Roca after that speech. He apologized stating that he is mainly here to answer any questions and again, the point of our membership is to advocate for them.  This is something that our membership voted on and in favor of doing and seeing carried out.  It is a mutually beneficial benefit for the city of Allentown as well as the members of the Queen City FOP.\par
\par
Chief Charles Roca stated if there are any questions, they will be happy to take any questions in financial matters that he would defer to finance to answer some of that.  \par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stat ok and thanks for that and they can and if any of his colleagues wants to ask questions.  Tonight was more informational for us and they are going to continue to develop questions and thoughts on this, but in the meantime if anybody has any questions, you are welcome to ask now.  He stated go ahead Mr. Pungo.\par
\par
Mr. Cristian Pungo stated that he is just one thing not necessarily a question, but more so a clarification.  He thinks for the folks who may watch this back in the future and to the folks here and they talked about the DROP Program, but maybe can we have basic terms to explain how it functions and what it actually does.    \par
\par
Chief Charles Roca stated so essentially when an officer decides to enter the DROP, they have to meet the (inaudible) number which is (inaudible) years of service to the Police Department.  They can achieve that a couple of ways serving the full 20 year s or let's say they have some military time, they can buy back military time so if they are 18 years on the job, they can purchase two years of service time of military time to bring that to 20.  Once they hit that 20 years, they may enter the DROP Pension for five years and within that five years, they can stay up to that amount, but at that point they can and they essentially, their Pension payments get put in a bucket account for them and they get paid by the city so they still get compensated as working the job and their pension is actually at that time.  They are retired, but they are still in active service.  When they officer decides to retire after two, three, four or five years, they will get a lump sum payment based upon that in addition to their pension or any 457 contributions which is a separate investment account that they can pay into.\par
\par
Sergeant Chris Matthews stated that if he could just add so their Pension while they are continuing to work for the city for up to 60 months.  That money stays into the Pension Fund itself so it will continue to accrue interest in which benefits the Pension Fund as well and it is only upon its separation that money gets pulled out of that fund and on top of that, their Pension is logged in at a 20 year rate as opposed to even if they stayed at an additional five years, their Pension is not recalculated for a 25 year Pension.  It stays at the lower amount for the 20 year Pension instead of 25.\par
\par
Chief Charles Roca stated that the permits will change if they were hired before 2009 and if they were a 23 year veteran and they decide to enter, the Pension will be ata 23 year Pension based upon that per 2009 Pension numbers.  \par
\par
Mr. Cristian Pungo stated thank you for the clarification for the folks who may not know.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated ok, Ms. Santos.\par
\par
Ms. Natalie Santos asked are officers able to switch Pension Plans.  She asked is that what we are trying to do here to get them to them to get them.\par
 \par
Chief Charles Roca stated that what happens here is that we have a Defined Pension so after they serve a certain amount of time, they are eligible for that Pension.  What a DROP Pension or Deferred Retirement Option, allows that officer to technically be retired or continually actively work for the Police Department. It is the fact that you don't lose their experience in time for serving the department.   That's when the benefit comes in.  \par
\par
Ms. Natalie Santos stated thank you.\par
\par
Chief Charles Roca stated that you are welcome.  \par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated Ms. Gerlach, go ahead.  \par
\par
Ms. Ce Ce Gerlach stated two questions, what potentially could be some of the downsides to doing this.  There are always pluses and sometimes there are downsides.  \par
\par
Chief Charles Roca stated that there are sometimes downsides if they are not properly tracked through Finance and things like that, it could put things at risks.  He stated that is why he was advocating and Deferred to our Finance people kind of talk about the Finances so you can have a full understanding what the MMO obligation is and the Municipal Obligation and how that rise in different scenarios.  \par
\par
Ms Ce Ce Gerlach stated that she doesn't see Bina or Ms. Patel.\par
\par
Mr. Frank Kane stated that Bina is off this week. She is caring for her elderly parents.\par
\par

Please observe the Rules of Council when addressing the body. A full copy of Council Rules can be found on the city website or by email if you contact Council office. 

There are multiple opportunities to address Council. Individuals can speak during Courtesy of the Floor (addressing items not on the agenda) and during Bills and Resolutions on Final Passage and Introduction. When given the Floor, please go to the podium and state your name and address. All remarks must be directed towards the presiding officer or council as a body; not a particular Council member or elected official, the audience or city staff. Unless otherwise determined, individuals shall have three minutes to address council and individuals representing a bona-fide group shall have five minutes. Privilege of the Floor will not be extended for personal insults or personal attacks on any individual, name calling or other behavior that is inconsistent with the purpose and intent of conducting official business. Please address council as a body. Refrain from using offensive language, cursing and making noises while other people are speaking. Act with decorum. Remove your hat and turn cell phones off. 

(Council Speaking Rules: Members and others given the privilege of the floor will address the Presiding Officer.  The Presiding Officer will extend the courtesy to the Councilperson(s) responsible for introducing legislation the opportunity to speak first.  Each member will have the right to speak twice on any subject.  No Member will be allowed to speak more than twice on any subject without permission of the Presiding Officer. He stated so we are going to move along to Courtesy of the Floor stating that this is an opportunity for members of the public to speak on any item that is not on our agenda on this evenings so if there is something further along on the agenda that you wish to speak on, let's just wait for that portion of the agenda, but if there is anything else that is city related, you have three minutes and asked if they have any Courtesy of the Floor speakers.\par
\par
Mr. Michael Hanlon stated no.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated ok.  He stated so we are going to move along to Contract Approvals.  He stated that we are going to start with R82.\par
}

Please observe the Rules of Council when given privilege of the floor. A copy of the Council Rules can be found on the council agenda on the website. If you would like to speak, we are asking that you fill out a card – they are on the back table provide them to the clerk before speaking. Include your name and address. When speakers have the privilege of the floor, personal insults, attacks, name calling or other behavior that is inconsistent with the purpose of conducting official business will not be tolerated.

Courtesy of the Floor is meant to provide public comments on items that are not on the agenda. Public comment during consideration of ordinances, resolutions and motions are limited by topic – your comments must be relevant to the subject matter of the proposed legislation. Public comments are taken before 	council votes on legislation. 

You are given the privilege of the floor to provide public comment; it is not a question and answer session. State your position clearly and concisely for consideration. If you speak on behalf of yourself, you have three minutes and if you are speaking on behalf of a group that has several members present, you will be given five minutes in place of everyone coming to the podium. Please address the Council President not individual councilpersons or city staff. Refrain from insulting or defaming staff, officials, and the public; refrain from using offensive language, cursing, and making noises while other people are speaking. Please be aware that comments and/or behavior in violation of these rules will result in a forfeiture of all remaining time and you will be asked to return to your seat
