\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Mr. Santo Napoli stated ok and thank you.  He stated and to be clear, his colleagues received an updated version of this.  He stated that they got some feedback from the public and made some updates to the Bill and there was some updates that were shared earlier today with his colleagues so everyone should have the newer version. He stated so we will get started on this and stated that he is going to point to the administration first to see if they are any comments or they will start with the questions and comments from the dais.\par
\par
Mr. Frank Kane asked Heidi is she had any comments.\par
\par
Ms. Heidi Westerman stated that she didn't want to yell because it is scary.  She stated so this ordinance has come up as you know they want to have an actual list of Vacant Properties in the city of Allentown.    In the past, they required them to do the at risk grant registration which doesn't tell them exactly what properties are vacant so often times their emergency personnel would be going into buildings they don't know if they are vacant or they should be vacant.  She stated that they have squatters and have people breaking into buildings and things like that so they are hoping that Council will consider this ordinance tonight to help them maintain a record of what is vacant in the city and also allows them to conduct an inspection of the properties that are vacant and allow them to see what is being stored in there, what is going on in the properties, and making sure they are properly secured.  He stated ok, thank you.\par
\par
Ms. Vicky Kistler stated that they had several episodes recently that had led to our concern about this ordinance that she thinks that Council needs to hear.  She stated thank you, Frank.  She stated that they had first responders entering properties for an extended period of time and finding propane tanks and large numbers of the roof of the building on fire, hazard materials stored in vacant properties that pose additional risks to those responders. They also had responders spending significant time in vacant properties looking for occupants, only to learn later that they haven't been occupants in years so that's one of our concerns.  The second concern is that the vacant properties in the neighborhood lower property values for all of our neighbors that live there and they often assigned for the use of disportionate city services where they respond to the same vacant property numerous times so the registry will hopefully allow us to share that information among our first responders, if they are responding to a property, but also to help us get a handle on where they do have occupants and they need to respond perhaps in a different way.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated ok, thank you.  He stated that it might be a good idea maybe for them to talk about some of the changes that were made just so that the public is brought up to speed on some of the updates and we will continue the conversation if any other comments come up, but he knows one thing that was a big change was they eliminated At Risk and put it all into one Bill which is the vacant property registry so help us out.\par
\par
Ms. Vicky Kistler stated that she wants to commend Heidi, she has written this Ordinance six times and they have taken feedback from anyone and everyone who has offered them feedback and tried to accommodate as much as possible so she is going to let Heidi highlight the changes, most which came from either from Council input or from citizens or community partners input.\par
\par
Ms. Heidi Westerman stated sure, some of the changes that they considered and as they said they had an At Risk registration requirement for the city, she is not quite sure what year it started, but it wasn't a true Vacant Property Registry.  They wanted to see properties that were in foreclosure, but you know people paid their mortgage and then they are no longer on the list.  It is not really vacant.  They wanted to have a real idea of what was vacant in the city so by eliminating that requirement of the At Risk and just truly having a vacant property ordinance and feel (inaudible) what they are trying to accomplish here. They are willing to remove that from the requirements of registration which is a change from the original ordinance.  She stated that they also cleaned up as a recommendation from the realtors association.  She thanked everyone for reviewing it and put in and cleared up hopefully what is considered occupied and what was considered vacant.  She stated that they want to make sure that they are not capturing properties like they have people that are like snowbirds and people that are temporarily out of their homes due to military deployment or hospitalizations.  This is not what we are trying to do.  They are clearing up the language here that they are not capturing those people that there was no reason for them to actually register since it is technically still owner occupied.  The people may be just temporarily out of the home for some reason and also to and they did put some language in here that would eliminate the requirement for the fee. It would still require people to register, but the fee is waived if they completed a presale inspection.   So for properties that are currently listed for sale or something like that completed the presale inspection where the property is compliant.  They were asking them to and if it is more than 30 days vacant as part of the calls us up and let us know and put it on the registry.  She stated that they are aware it is vacant as they are driving through the city.    She stated that they know it is a vacant property so we see people coming in and out the front door and you know that they are not supposed to be there.  Those are all important things, but we don't want to have them to have to register something twice or pay a fee twice.   They already completed the presale.  They are compliant.  The properties are maintained.  She stated that they just want to know if it is going to be vacant for a long period of time.  She stated that she is trying to think of some of the other changes.\par
\par
Ms. Vicky Kistler stated some of the other changes and one of the other changes is that currently the DCED Director can waive fees in DCED.  It is rare that they do, but there are certain circumstances that require them to consider waiving fees.  She stated that she did not change that she will make the call or her designee could make the call in her absence because they don't want this to be an onerous process people.  Originally a suggestion was made that this all goes to the blighted property review committee.  She stated that she would hate to see that happen and the reason she would hate to see that happen is that if someone is on active military duty and they call her or email her and can verify that's true, why should they have to appear before a committee.  They commit to a committee and wait for a committee meeting.  They should be able to give and instantaneous response to a person that is temporarily in a Rehab Facility or somebody who is snowbirding.  She does however appreciates the fact that they don't want to be the soul entity in a department making a decision so they put in a provision that any decision that she makes that no one likes could be appealed to the Blighted Property Review Committee and then that would be a more extensive process or to Lehigh County Court if they truly didn't approve of what we did, but she would like to be able to make a very easy process for people who are on vacation, snowboarding/snowbirding or whatever you want to deal with the snow.  Military duty or whatever that temporary leave that exonerates your fee.  It should be able to be a very easy common sense decision and not appearing before a board.\par
\par
Ms. Heidi Westerman stated two other things, it was good catch on there end where the public nuisance part of it stating that they had it listed that all At Risk and Vacant Properties would be immediately cleared of public nuisance and she is not quite sure why they have that there because she just will refer it back to 406.2 which is the public nuisance definition of a vacant/abandon property and the last thing was there was some comment on 611-11 imposing or obstructing enforcement officers.  They were just referring back to the IPMC which gives them the Right of Entry requirements and she thinks that was pretty much it.    \par
\par
Ms. Vicky Kistler stated that she thinks it covers most of it.  \par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated ok, thank you.  This is nice to hear the updates so that everyone on the same page.  He stated that he appreciates them calling out the days and stated so that said for his colleagues and asked if there are any questions or comments.  He stated Mr. Binder, go ahead.\par
\par
Mr. Jeremy Binder stated for the administrative guidelines.  He stated that he knows that they talked about the scoring matrix for that.  The last time they were here and asked what is the administrative guidelines look like.  He stated that he knows they are referencing it, but what do you feel that is going to look like.  \par
\par
Ms. Heidi Westerman asked so are you saying as far as our determination of the vacancy that you are referring to.\par
\par
Ms. Vicky Kistler stated that he is referring to the fact that we are going to be developing a criteria that says that we have an inspector who actually viewed the property that they have conditions that indicate vacancy such as overgrown weeds, abandoned vehicles that have overgrowth on them.  Broken windows, a hole in the roof, no one answering our calls, no one answering and our knocks on the door.  They will have that all spelled out and our administrative training with a staff who is taking on these responsibilities.  They pretty much do this already.  They pretty much have a constant back and forth banter between the inspectors in the field and the Mr. Shahda and Heidi are the two managing personnel within the department.  It is pretty obvious just to determine that it is vacant.  They also speak to neighbors.  They also ask if anybody seen anyone coming or going.  Oftentimes the indicators are right there and they are accumulation of mail.  The fact that they may hear barking dogs, but knock on the door repetitively and no one answers the door.  She state that there are abandon animals so those will be some of the criterias.  They are interested in tagging properties that are for sale if they are vacant, however, if they remain vacant for extended period of time, the city ask them to register and ask that they have an active activity that they can see that they are trying to have showings or trying to actively market the property none the less.  They do have staff who have access to the MLS that they can check to make sure the property is listed as an active sale and those will all be in our criteria.    \par
\par
Mr. Jeremy Binder stated thank you, is the and stated that he knows this will be public and he understands the E Code.  He asked is there a Plan for those guidelines to actually be public or where will those live.  It is something someone could reference that they are looking for.  \par
\par
Ms. Heidi Westerman stated that they will add it to the city's website as well of that information pertaining to this and the E Code.  \par
\par
Mr. Jeremy Binder stated ok, thank you.  He stated Ms. Gerlach, go ahead.\par
\par
Ms. Ce Ce Gerlach stated building off of that it doesn't look like it shouldn't have to be too much to do to develop that because it looks like Fannie Mae and she knows, they have issues, but Fannie Mae, the USDA has already have their metrics is out there that kind of assess vacant properties.  She stated that is great.  She stated but, then she had two questions.   She stated that she doesn't see page numbers where it is talking about commercial properties and asked could you explain the rationale of taking out this specific language like what's been crossed out as an old vacant storefront shall maintain adequate lighting and then, not allow graffiti, and remove it.  Property owners still have to maintain that level.  What was the thinking of not requiring commercials. \par
\par
Ms. Heidi Westerman asked are you referring to the vacant storefront.  Where they crossout.\par
\par
Ms. Ce Ce Gerlach stated yes.  \par
\par
Ms. Heidi Westerman stated that one of the thing that they originally were going to request that the windows will be covered and it wouldn't track people like looking into it.  She asked what will we be doing as it was brought to our attention is creating more of a pr oblem because wouldn't be able to see in the window and it could create opportunities to break into the back door and be living in there and nobody could look in there and see through the window so they kind of like revised that and the commercial buildings have to maintain and still have to file the Property Maintenance Code so remember this ordinance goes hand and hand IPMC so everything that is required in the International Property Maintenance Code is going to be required of all of these buildings regardless and some of these are and this ordinance is just for the registration, but everything we are inspecting and requiring of that vacant property is going to fall under the International Property Maintenance Code, if that makes sense.\par
\par
Ms. Ce Ce Gerlach stated yeah, that makes sense.  She stated ok, now in terms of data sharing she knows it tends to be a lot of systems and sometimes the systems don't interact.  If a property is labeled as vacant within CED, how does that get into an EMS worker or a police officer and they work with a different system.  How does that get to them?  \par
\par
Ms. Heidi Westerman stated that we work hand and hand like with the Fire Marshal and things like that.  They have access.  \par
\par
Ms. Ce Ce Gerlach stated that they are on the way.  How do they find out live?  Are they going to text someone or?\par
\par
Ms. Heidi Westerman stated some of them do have access to our Intergov System.  She believes because she knows Fire Marshall Steed and her work hand and hand with these properties.  She stated that they can lookup information.  It could have that notation that it would be a vacant property.  It will also would have anything that would be listed in there that could be of danger or if there is something being stored there in the property, like propane tanks.  She said there was a property that they had a fire at on N. 10th Street one year and it was a vacant property and on the roof of that property was all of these stored propane tanks.  Firemen are running into that building that is on fire now and they don't know top of that building is propane tanks.  These are things that if they had eyes on the vacant property, they would know that this property is vacant and if we seen something like that it would be reporting those different things to the Fire Marshal as well.\par
\par
Ms. Ce Ce Gerlach stated so you are saying as the police, as the EMS, the ambulance, as the fire trucks are rushing to the scene and they are going to go on Intergov and see if and asked how would they and stated that she guesses if they are going to do this and this is for public safety.\par
 \par
Ms. Heidi Westerman stated that they have a once a month meeting of problem properties. If they had a property that was vacant and had Code violations such as that.  She stated that was brought up at the meetings so that is brought to their attention before that fire even happens.  She stated that they already aware of those are things that are being notations on and what system that they use that they would put information and red flags on that so that becomes where it pops up of their screen while they are driving to the fire, if that makes sense, you know.\par
\par
Ms. Vicky Kistler stated also the have a simultaneous callout system.  So when there is a fire, Heidi is sent the alert that there is a fire as well as their staff respond to support the fire or the police on their building related calls so information can be verbally shared by the onsite building inspector without them, but anything that would strike them as an emergency as Heidi said during the problem property meetings would be shared or instantaneously.  An inspector comes back and finds that they have and this has happened in an abandoned laboratory that has chemicals of an unknown origin stored in the building.  Immediately, the Fire Marshal's are contacted.  They do an immediate inspection.  They flag the building on their hazmat.  She stated she them getting in and our eyes on the buildings will get them to flag them in their systems so that they can add hazardous materials. They can add a ton of information that can be shared from our inspections, directly into their callout screens.\par
\par
Ms. Ce Ce Gerlach stated that it just will be interesting to see operationally how it works.  \par
\par
Ms. Vicky Kistler stated that they agree stating that this is a PILOT so that is one of the things that we are going to discuss.  Right now, we are still going to siloed because police information data has different firewalls and shareability then our data does.  Our Police Department is not in Intergov and our Fire Department has a Fire Marshal in Intergov, but we do not have Police in Intergov so its beholding on us to make sure they have the information that they need and that's why they have these Command Meetings, these Public Safety meetings and these problem property meetings to share that information that ahead of time.  \par
\par
Ms. Ce Ce Gerlach stated ok and then.\par
\par
Ms. Vicky Kistler stated that they also going to call them.  If they arrive at a building against one of them that has a Building Standards flag for hazardous materials.   It is going to be a trigger to call the owner and the on call person which they do now typically on scale emergencies.    \par
\par
Ms. Ce Ce Gerlach stated ok, then the next then what?  Some cities declare it a public nuisance and then that triggers like a receivership and then Sidney can designate a nonprofit to purchase that property and now we can now.\par
\par
Ms. Heidi Westerman stated so this ordinance is now referencing that public nuisance ordinance is already established.  A public nuisance property, those are properties where let's say we can't get a hold of the owner.  We tried to do enforcement, but the front porch is going to collapse.  at some point,  if we determine an immediate Public Safety and we are going to take that porch down.  We are going to then lien the property.  That's like the public nuisance ordinance is for them to act when something is a danger or immediate danger to the public.  \par
\par
Ms. Vicky Kistler stated that there are two different types of Nuisance Declarations.  One is declaring a public nuisance which means they have time.  They can follow their protocols to contact the property owner, work on an abatement program, discuss ways that they can remedy to situation.  Then there is an emergent public nuisance and an emergent public nuisance means that we that we have an immediate lifesaving issue.  The roof is falling in, the wall is collapsing, there is a huge raging party going on that have violence associated with it.  If they declare an immediate emergent public nuisance, they can have an all disciplinary team response.  She stated that they can actually padlock a building and cut utilities if we have to whether or not the owner is present.  If it qualifies to meet emergent and there is then the idea that an emergent or non-emergent public nuisance fails to cooperate with us, we can actually build all of the response and emergency personnel or not to the property owner and if they do not pay for that response once they can lien the property.  That can be appealed to the Nuisance Board of Appeals here in city hall.   They had one yesterday or that can be appealed to the Lehigh County Courts to say that they acted in an appropriately.\par
\par
Ms. Ce Ce Gerlach stated ok.  She stated that she appreciates the changes.  She stated that she thinks it makes it less likely not to and it is not likely completely impossible, but less likely to have an unintended consequence.   She stated that she knows that she went up to doors where it kind of looks vacant, but turns out it is just depressed and didn't feel like checking the mail and you know.\par
\par
Ms. Vicky Kistler stated that they find that and hoping they can  offer some help or we can offer some services to them or try to send to check the welfare for them.   She stated that is another reason and it is very important that they be able to kind of get a handle on where they have folks who need our help as well as folks who has just left and abandoned the property.\par
\par
Ms. Ce Ce Gerlach stated thank you.  She stated that is all she has, thank you.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated if there is any other questions or comments from the dias.  He stated that one question and stated that we going to have situations where folks sell properties so less say we have a property on the vacant property registry and that property is sold.  He asked can you explain what happened.  Just like a hypothetical date.  \par
\par
Ms. Heidi Westerman stated that if the property was on the vacant property list and somebody purchases that property, they would have gotten a presale so that's why the presale waiving is including in that.  If it was vacant and she purchased the property, it would have been required prior to the presale.  The presale is good for one year so you wouldn't have to register.   Now, after that year is up and you never occupied the property, they would expect that you either going to apply to another presale or you are going to register the property that is vacant.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated that hypothetically, what could the next person do.  What would trigger staying off of the registry.  Starting a rehab, permits being pulled, what triggers it.\par
\par
Ms. Heidi Westerman stated that there is a couple of different things that is going to require that some of them are going to be required to register because you know because if they are vacant for more than 90 days, but if it is a reason behind it and for example you submitted plans and pulled permits and actively doing construction.  She stated that she doesn't expect them to register it as a vacant property or pay the fee for the vacant property.  If you are just trying to get it sold, you paid for your presale and you completed the inspection and you completed the and corrected all of the violations and now the property is just sitting there and just having a hard time selling for whatever reason.  We would only expect you to pay a fee to register a property.  There were different things that would require you and still would want to know if it was vacant like she said and we don't necessarily need you to pay a fee.  She stated that they are not going to do the inspection and the presale was already just done.\par
\par
Ms. Vicky Kistler stated that if you think about it, do we expect someone to be in that property.  If a property is on the market and actively being marketed, we can expect that at any given time somebody could be going through for a showing.  That's fine.  That's not a vacant property, but if a property is on the market for a year or a year and a half and they never had a showing, they haven't adjusted the price.  The property has been empty and stated that they just want to get their eyes on what is in that property and want to let folks know that they can enter that property knowing that they shouldn't expect anybody to be there.  If they are seeing signs that they are drug activity or legal activity going on in this property, we don't think it should be there at the time.  Contact the property owner and find out is that supposed to be there.  Just don't walk the other way and thinking it's supposed to be an occupied building.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated ok and regarding the fees that you mentioned. He stated that this is all rental funds, right.  He asked is that correct.  He asked is that Enterprise Fund.   \par
\par
Ms. Heidi Westerman stated yes, that is Rental, yes.  That is Enterprise Fund.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated ok and you based the fees stating he guesses they based the fees om the amount of service provided or the amount of resources.  \par
\par
Ms. Heidi Westerman stated that is correct.  The money that comes into the Rental Fund is based on the Rental Registration fees.   She stated that we don't ever capture is all the work that goes into The Code Enforcement, the time, paperwork, the constant driving by the property or calling out the board up company and the constant enforcement and actions that are required for these properties.  She stated that they don't ever recapture that expense.  Sometime they can have properties that are vacant for multiple years and they might board that same property up like 30 times in a year because people will keep breaking in.  She stated that it is nothing right now that is currently helping them fund that enforcement action so they are hoping that it would help offset some of that costs.  \par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated ok, that said he thinks the residentials are too high.  He stated that he looks at residentials versus commercial.  He stated that he thinks right now, they have it as 200 and 300.  He stated that he can see maybe residential maybe being half so that is something they can talk about rather than lowering the residential fee maybe to 150 just to make it half of commercial.  He stated that is something that he would be in favor of, but ultimately, when he looks at the legislation and obviously we can read it, but to him it is about what's the spirit of it and what are you trying to accomplish.    He stated that he thinks what he is hearing is and what he is hearing and what he think he is hearing correct.  It is really about just holding vacant property owners accountable and making sure that, again we are not talking about short-term vacancy, but we are talking about long-term:  two years, three years, five years.  There are vacancies in city for tenure.  He stated just making sure that these vacant properties are not affecting your neighbors.  He stated that we hear stories from Council all the time about a vacant property causing damage to a homeowners property next door and homeowners are really frustrated because the owners not assessable and no one knows who to call and because it is vacant, it's one of the reasons vacant property insurance is so high because it is no one there to actually report any of it so it becomes a small issue becomes a big issue.  He stated no one knows about it during that time frame so he thinks it is really important to get eyes on these properties to understand the issues for if you are sharing it with public safety which he thinks is important if you are having these meetings and you are sharing the database to properties that are of concern. That is great news, but it is really about protecting homeowners and other property owners from some of these vacant properties that are calling issues.  Lastly, he would say we talked about blighted properties a lot and know it is an ongoing issue. He believes vacant properties ultimately are the next generation of blighted properties.  He stated not all vacant properties.  He stated that he doesn't want to tag them all together, but he believes there are vacant properties that were left vacant for a decade or 15 years.  They become the next blighted properties in the city.  So can we get eyes on it and can we make sure that repairs are made and keep it from becoming blighted.  He stated it is a lot cheaper when you do it that way versus trying to rehab a blighted property that has reached a point of no return stating that he thinks that is important.    \par
\par
Ms. Vicky Kistler stated that they really want the properties activated an they really can't stress to you enough and how they can't stress with them enough how routine work of them getting into systematic inspections get hindered because the staff gets so tied up in complaint based work and it's not like we want the complaints, but they get complaints constantly about the squirrels in the attic of the connecting wall.  The roaches that are coming through the vacant property wall into the inhabited row house.  The fact that she is terrified because there are constantly people breaking into the house next door and she is afraid if they set a fire they are going to lose their home.  Those are the things that these inspectors are going out on constantly and when they get to the property, they have no idea who belongs there.   Because when they enter the property or not to enter the property and someone answers the door, it is logical expectation that is the property or illegal tenant, but if they have the property owner telling them that that property supposed to be vacant.  She stated that we know who is opening the door who doesn't belong there and that's where we make the phone call to be able to say hey, we changed and missed the registry or you got people living in this property and a lot of this has to do with landlords that are not local and they haven't had eyes. agenda_items.title:
Bill 50 
Amending the 2026 General Fund budget to accommodate the upgrade of the Opioid Prevention Manager and the Health Director in the Bureau of Health within the Department of Community & Economic Development.  The Opioid Prevention Manager, currently an s09, would be upgraded to a proposed pay grade of s11 to align with the similar levels of responsibility, autonomy and workload as five (5) other s11’s in the Bureau. The permanent wages of this position are fully grant funded. The Health Director, currently an s18, would be upgraded to a proposed pay grade of s21 to acknowledge the addition of three (3) new program areas since the position was last graded in 2017 and the cabinet level responsibilities of this position while remaining in the supervisory pay scale. This position is partially grant funded.

Bill 51 
Amending the 2026 General Fund budget to accommodate the downgrade and title change of the vacant Grants Compliance Administrator to an Assistant Grants Compliance Administrator in the Bureau of CDBG Administration within the Department of Community & Economic Development.  The Grants Compliance Administrator, currently an s11, would be downgraded to a proposed pay grade of s07 to align with the level of responsibility, autonomy and workload that the office currently needs for this vacant position. The permanent wages of this position are 60% HUD grant reimbursable and 40% General Fund funded.
June 3, 2026 City Council Meeting Minutes

The purpose of this Special Meeting is to review a citizen initiative. Under the city's Home Rule Charter citizens who officially gather the necessary signature of Allentown residents may introduce or repeal legislation may have special meetings and may place items to the Council Agenda for discussion.  On June 22, 2026, Council Clerk sent a memo to Council determining that the Citizens Petition with the signatures submitted, was significant.  President Napoli then placed the item on the next available agenda which occurred on July 15th and then he scheduled this meeting.  She stated that she wants to thank the Petitioners Committee and the circulators for their work in gathering the requirement signatures as well as our staff for the close review of the petitions.  The citizens initiative process parallels that legislative bill, however, if Council does not adopt the proposed the citizens evaluation moves forward to Lehigh County for placement on the next municipal election ballot, allowing voters to decide via a referendum process so this evening, they will proceed as they typically do with legislative matters.  She stated hearing first from the Petitioners, followed by comments from the administration and then Council and then the public.  After the discussion, they will entertain a Motion from any Councilmember who wishes to offer one so now they are ready.  They would like to hear from the Petitioner.\par
\par

\par

\par

She stated while she was working in a warehouse in the Lehigh Valley, she faced a situation where she was ill with a throat infection, a fever and very high blood pressure.  She stated at the time, she was working in a warehouse where missing a shift was resulted in accumulation of points that would lead to her termination. She stated that on another occasion, her daughter was sick, yet she could not stay home with her even though she was very ill with vomiting and intestinal pain because missing work could have resulted in her being fired.  Working Class families like hers have been faced with deciding between our health and our families and being able to keep up with our bills for years.  She stated that this initiative will give all workers across the city regardless of income or race, the ability to take care of their families and themselves without fear of losing their paycheck or their job.  She collected signatures for the Petition to get this on the ballot.  Residents from across the city of Allentown express joy to learn about the possibility of having paid sick days.  The opportunity to be able to care for sick children and not get other six at work without fear of losing their paycheck or job would be a great relief.  She stated that she looks forward to the opportunity to voice her support for this initiative at the polls in November.   Thank you. She stated that as you are aware, this ordinance was brought to you as a Charter Citizen Initiative Referendum.  It was not proposed by the city of Allentown's city administration, Allentown's City Council, any administrative board, commission or third party agency that functions under the health bureau or Lehigh County.  As such, there is no research, investigations, studies or data collected by the city or the city affiliated public health organization that shows the ordinance should protect the public health or assist in disease prevention and control.  There are currently over 20,500 active in city license businesses that the Health Bureau would be required to monitor for compliance and enforcement.  The city does not currently have staffing or administrative processes in place to comply with this ordinance. Implementation of this ordinance would require significant investment and additional staffing which may result in doubling or tripling the city's business license fees and/or property tax increase.  The measures will be in addition to the cost of the businesses after this benefit.  She stated finally many of the people who live in Allentown, do not work in Allentown and many people who work in  Allentown live elsewhere. Please observe the Rules of Council when addressing the body. A full copy of Council Rules can be found on the city website or by email if you contact Council office. 

There are multiple opportunities to address Council. Individuals can speak during Courtesy of the Floor (addressing items not on the agenda) and during Bills and Resolutions on Final Passage and Introduction. When given the Floor, please go to the podium and state your name and address. All remarks must be directed towards the presiding officer or council as a body; not a particular Council member or elected official, the audience or city staff. Unless otherwise determined, individuals shall have three minutes to address council and individuals representing a bona-fide group shall have five minutes. Privilege of the Floor will not be extended for personal insults or personal attacks on any individual, name calling or other behavior that is inconsistent with the purpose and intent of conducting official business. Please address council as a body. Refrain from using offensive language, cursing and making noises while other people are speaking. Act with decorum. Remove your hat and turn cell phones off. 

(Council Speaking Rules: Members and others given the privilege of the floor will address the Presiding Officer.  The Presiding Officer will extend the courtesy to the Councilperson(s) responsible for introducing legislation the opportunity to speak first.  Each member will have the right to speak twice on any subject.  No Member will be allowed to speak more than twice on any subject without permission of the Presiding Officer.  No Member will speak more than three (3) times on the question without the unanimous consent of all the Members present.

If we wanted to make amendments to Bill 20 at that at that time, it would have to go through the entire process all over again, which leaves which would leave no regulations in place. agenda_items.title:
Bill 52
Amending Part II General Legislation, Chapter 660 Zoning, Article 5 Uses, Table 660-4 Use Table and Section 660-38 Manufacturing & Industry Group, adding public notice requirements and amending the use category Data Center Use.

NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING

Notice is hereby given that the Allentown City Council will consider for possible adoption an Ordinance Amending Part II General Legislation, Chapter 660 Zoning, Article 5 Uses, Table 660-4 Use Table and Section 660-38 Manufacturing & Industry Group, adding public notice requirements and amending the use category Data Center Use, in order to increase setback requirements, remove the data center use from the IG zone, revise noise and vibration standards, and create new standards for decommissioning.

City Council will consider the foregoing at a Public Hearing on Wednesday, August 5, 2026 at 6:00 PM in Council Chambers, 435 Hamilton Street, Allentown, PA 18101. Copies of the full text of this Ordinance are available to any interested party for examination and copying at the City Clerk’s Office or for inspection during regular business hours at the offices of this newspaper and the Lehigh County Department of Law. All documents can also be found on the City website. City Council may adopt this amendment to the Zoning Ordinance at the regularly scheduled City Council Meeting at 6:30 PM on August 5, 2026 immediately following this Public Hearing.

There was a state match at one point which made it was $36,000. If you were eligible, you needed a 600 credit score, and if you didn't have it, the banks were enrolling you in their financial literacy and credit rating improvement program, which was a six to eight week online and in-person partnership. And if you completed that whole series, they disregarded your credit score and gave you a shot at it. Our problem continues to be them in the bidding war, getting the property.  Because what happens is they get certified, they get the state money, they get ready for the appraisal, they get ready for the down payment, and they don't get the cash. I mean, they don't get the house because of the cash bid that comes from New York or New Jersey. So we have one. We have one that did it that we know is flourishing, but one so controlling that inventory and why the Housing Authority Program is so special is because they're controlling that property ownership. So they're controlling who gets that property by the 80%, AMI? That's the beauty. That's what DCED would love to be able to do. That's what we're working with RACA to try to do. That's why we're writing grants to purchase properties. But as he's saying, when you use that federal money, when you use any of our money, it triggers all of the expensive rehab using Davis-Bacon, having BABA (sp), having supply chain, all of the things prevailing wages that drive up the cost of the rehab. But we're so grateful for the opportunity. And I just want to share that every citizen who wants to buy a house who struggles with income, if they can become bankable, they're positioned for whatever program he has or whatever program we come up with. So we are trying to drive people to banks, even if they think they aren't close to being ready to try to work on getting ready. Thank you. \par
\par
Mr. Julio Guridy stated that I would just add to that, that the Community Action has a Program for first time homebuyer classes that they do, and it's a great program. I mean, it's been going on. I was on the board for 12 years back in the 80s and early 90s. And we actually translated, I actually translated into Spanish back in those days. So you can you can do it in Spanish or English and they help you. I gone over to them. They usually meet on a Saturday morning, I think it's 8:00 in the morning. I think they meet and they and I went over to talk to the class.   There were about 35 people there about some of the properties that we have that they can acquire, they can get as long as they're having their own house for five years at least, because first time homebuyer, sometimes I think it used to be 10, but I think we're going down to five years. They can apply for this because we're not we're looking for first time home buyers, not somebody who buys a house or rents out to somebody else, okay. And sometimes that happens with people just want to like stay there for buy the house cheap and then move out in a year or two and rent it out or sell it, flip it. We're not into that. We want first time homebuyers to live there and stay for at least five, 10.  We say 10 years. but, you know, things happen sometimes to people. So, okay. \par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\sa160\sl276\slmult1\kerning2\f0\fs24 Mr. Santo Napoli stated okay. Well, thank you again. We appreciate it. And okay, moving along. Our second presentation is from the downtown Allentown alliance. We have some members here. Their Executive Director, Ms. Lisa Finkelstein. We have their Chair, Mr. Matthew Mallozzi, and their Vice Chair, Mr. Kyle Edwards. So thank you for joining us. And you can take it away. Thank you. \par
\par
Mr. Matt Mallozzi stated thank you, Council members. We appreciate your time and allowing us to come in and give you an update on what we've been up to and answer your questions. Is it okay if we distribute some of our presentations so that council can follow along? \par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated yeah. \par
\par
Mr. Matt Mallozzi stated thank you as Councilman Napoli introduced us. I\rquote m Matt Mallozzi. I serve as the Chair of the Board for the Downtown Allentown Alliance. I\rquote m joined with Vice Chair Kyle Edwards and our executive director, Lisa Finkelstein. We'll introduce ourselves, I guess, as some background information. Some of you may remember last year, we were here in late July of 2025. We've covered a lot of ground since then, and that's what we're here to tell you about. Personally, I from Allentown, I was born and raised on the east side of Allentown and went to Moser and Harrison Morton and Dieruff, and I\rquote m an engineer. I work on Hamilton Street at Sixth and Hamilton in Tower Six is where my office is located. Kyle, would you care to go? \par
\par
Mr. Kyle Edwards stated sure, sure. Kyle Edwards again proud. Allentown graduated from Dieruff myself grew up on the southside, but I ended up graduating from Dieruff. My parents actually met at Dieruff. So again, Allentonian through and through.  Grew up in a business household. My family owned a deli back in the day. I own and operate Inkwell, which is an arts incubator in downtown Allentown. I also own a true love story, which is an arts and entertainment business. But again, just excited to be here. \par
\par
Ms. Lisa Finkelstein stated and Lisa Finkelstein, the Executive Director. I am a Pennsylvanian, not an Allentown, though.  Born in Philadelphia and raised in northeastern Pennsylvania, most of my background was spent in the small business world in a family business, and then I purchased it from my parents and ran that for 10 years. And then I left that and went into the nonprofit world for eight years, and then moved to Florida for five years and worked as an Executive Director for a Main Street Program there before returning to the Lehigh Valley in December. So glad to be back. But a diverse background that I bring to this, this role. Thank you.\par
\par
Mr. Matt Mallozzi stated thank you. I will we be running the presentation or Council will just follow along on our hard copies. Thank you. I will I\rquote ll start off with some background. Bring some of the Council members who may have not been here last year or those who were may forget some of the details, but the, the genesis of the downtown Allentown Alliance began in 2024 with a steering committee that was convened to take a look at why the downtown. In spite of record levels of investment by many different public and private organizations, was lacking in activation and vibrancy that really should have should have been there and was, was apparently building, I recall before Covid and then everything stopped in Covid, but it just didn't come back. We lost that trajectory. So that steering committee, among other things, commissioned a Report by, by national consultants that was entitled the downtown Allentown revitalization and activation report. That is, we call it the Report. And that will be referred to multiple times throughout. That's, that's what that refers to. There was a 283 page document and assessment that compared Allentown to our peers of similar size, demographics, locations, background as industrial cities and what it found, among other things, is, you know, some, some things validated, some of our ideas is the city compared to our peers is clean and safe, but we have a perception problem. And one of the things lacking that they talked about, you know, in terms of retail vibrancy and community engagement tourism and just the vibrancy of downtown was focused on creating a unified brand, unifying the, the amenities that we have. And that was pointed out in the report, too, is for a city of our size to have the cultural and art institutions that, that we have were the envy of anybody our size. When you think down starting, you know, on fifth street with museum and symphony hall and the Baum School all the way up to the 12th street, there's just a list of, of amenities and institutions that, that we have. And yet the space in between just isn't, isn't filled with people, at least not regularly as, as it needs to be. So that was that was the mission. And Kyle and I were invited to get this organization formed and get it off the ground. We were given the report and that served as our strategic guide and has become our strategic plan. Pulling from the Report. And we spent we spent the last year actually, well, starting with the first four months, really pulling this organization together. There was nothing we had a Report and the support of a lot of folks, but we really had to put the organization together ourselves. So we one of the things that was most important, you know, and I as the chair and responsible for the governance of the organization at the end of the day, was to make sure that there were two characteristics that we didn't lose sight of. One, and building on our experience from the past, and along with Councilman Napoli, I served on the Hamilton district main street program and then its successor organization, the downtown Allentown business alliance, for a total of about ten years. So saw that there was there was a lot of hope, a lot of heart, a lot of effort, but the traction just wasn't getting there. So what were we going to do differently about it? So our organization had to be independent. It could not exist. It could not be funded by any single organization, whether public or private, whether the city or private sector or county or the state. And it could not exist for the benefit of any single organization as well, too. We have to protect our independence, real and perceived. And the second was it needed to be a true public private partnership. And if we could accomplish those two things, that's what's different about this organization. So we were extremely thoughtful and deliberate, and we took time getting out of the gate. Our first four months, roughly may through September of last year, talking to a lot of people, a number of focus groups and putting together a board. And we engaged the United Way of the Greater Lehigh Valley to help incubate the organization and put together all the governance, the bylaws, the boards outlining the committee structure, which we're building out right now, and basically all of our filings you can imagine we applied for and successfully obtained 501(C)(3) status and all of the requisite regulatory filings with the state. And the federal government and IRS and took care of all that and then moved into the three priorities we had for what we call a year zero are the branding, the activations, and our Hospitality Ambassador Program. So beginning in, I guess, November, big milestone where we had a launch of our ambassador program. And, and our Ambassadors are here tonight in the back of the room, Geraldo, Robert and Emmanuel and their manager, Jim. Jim, Jim's over there, Jim, that we're here tonight. So we launched in, in November of last year on Pell Plaza. And a public statement following that, we began some activations, sort of a test in November and December, some small activations. And by activations, I mean DAA doesn't want to be the show. We want to facilitate enhance the show. We want to capture people who are coming downtown, passing through, maybe going to a destination dinner, a show, shopping, whatever they're doing, or just walking through downtown. So we would activate to complement those things. Maybe it's music, maybe it's face painting and that's what we were doing in the fall, in December, while that was all going on, we also kicked off our branding campaign. We hired an outside consultant. We talked to them about our mission, and they spent December, January and February developing our brand and our brand style. What DAA was going to use to market the downtown locally and regionally as well to in a unified brand structure. So that was going through during that time in January, late January, we finished a recruiting campaign and we hired our, our permanent Executive Director, Lisa. So it's, it's worthy to remember that she's been here just over six months and as we get through our accomplishments, I think you'll see we accomplish a lot with her. And then in march, we began a, a longer activation series. We took off over the winter, January, February, which were bitter cold, and the Ambassadors were on the street that entire time. But in March, we kicked off our activations, which are running through present and will go through October of this year. We had our brand reveal in April at the Da Vinci science center in their. One of their main rooms there kicked that off in a in a public. Actually, it was by invitation only, but we invited all of our stakeholders, including Council and, and various other stakeholders for that brand reveal. In may, we finalized our neighborhood partnership program grant application, which was a lot of work. Those who have been involved with that and as, as validation, when you go out and you try to get private organizations to sign on at a level that is required for an NPP grant, they could see the governance, they could see what we had already put together and accomplished. They could see our Strategic Plan and that it was a very real organization. And that our organization really is, is a rising tide lifts all ships.   There isn't a single entity or organization along Hamilton street that we're focused on. We're focused on making them all more successful and working closely with the city. And Vicky and Mark, especially in June, we launched our website. In July, we hired our social media manager, and today we had a meeting with our Founders Council, which is it's a reconstitution of the old Downtown Allentown Community Development Initiative, or DACDI and the supporters for our NPP application. So that brings us up to, to basically this afternoon, present day with what we've accomplished. And I\rquote ll turn it over now to my colleagues to bring you through the rest, like some of the highlights of what I just talked about. And then also our goals for where we're going to go now. And again, we, we've just started year one, we finished year zero and now we're beginning year one, which is why we're back to tell you everything that we've accomplished with your support. Thank you. \par
\par
Mr. Kyle Edwards stated thank you, Matt. He's very good at keeping the timeline because I forget all the things we've been up to, but as matt alluded to, years zero, one and two are focused on building a sustainable organization to be truly representative of the Downtown District. And how do we do that? So we focus on the four pillars that's pulled directly from the Doris Report enhancement. I\rquote m sorry, enhanced, engagement, and vibrancy, inspire, loyalty and advocacy. Create a dynamic retail landscape and celebrate and elevate cultural heritage. We focus on those pillars because again, they help us build that Strategic Plan, which our committees are now being built behind the scenes working on that early activities like public space activations, deploying our ambassador team and developing a downtown brand to support those pillars by improving perceptions of safety, providing a welcoming and vibrant downtown. As we all know, downtown has so much to offer. It's that public perception that we're really combating.  Some other events that we also supported, we did the tree lighting ceremony. We supported that Liberty Bell dedication, the pop up community bike repair. We have some others listed in my notes here. One moment. Classics and Cruisers. So again, we supported that Blueprint by Jones on Ninth, which is to come. Flannel Fest by Room and Ward, Walking Parade, the Allentown Comedy Festival. So again, we're, we're out there really trying to create the community we all know we deserve. And, we're going to do that with some of this is the committee structure. Next slide please, if you don't mind. So the committee structure is based on the retail committee, program committee and the governance committee. So, again the retail we're going to address some of that vacancy we see on the ground floor. We hope to recruit businesses and not just recruit but curate businesses, remove some of the barriers from small business owners, advocacy funds, space, etc. And create a pathway for market vendors to share space to brick and mortar. So we have plans to start a market and incubate some of these smaller businesses and hopefully help them to not only build confidence, but give them an opportunity to go ahead and extend to a brick and mortar. The program committee, ensure events, embrace the diverse cultures, which again, we all know we have, especially in particularly the Hispanic Community and the surrounding neighborhoods, the strategic approach to events with the globe, the goal of driving pedestrian traffic into downtown businesses. Again, we want the downtown businesses to flourish, reinforce and spread the downtown identity. The diverse committee members brings a variety of skill sets and viewpoints to the table, which we'll touch on here in a bit. The governance charged with finding committee and board prospects, as well as board governance. Next slide please. So you'll see here we have about 34 individuals serving on the DAA board of committees, some of which are municipal, all the way to corporate. Thirteen members identify as non-white. So again, we want the boards to reflect the diversity of the downtown and really embrace that. That's a strength of ours. We communicate weekly with downtown businesses. Some are stretched a little thin. They cannot devote time to serving on a committee. However, we do have eight retail owners or business owners on the ground floor that serve at this time. One area where we could use your help and this is a small ask, is identifying residents that may want to participate, who have a willingness, maybe some expertise, show the energy and pizzazz that we hope will reflect what it is we do with the DAA. Next slide, please. So again from the Doris Report, that annual work plan was developed. So the Strategic Plan, the four pillars set that direction flow right into that annual work plan, which again strategy strategizes the mapped to the pillars. So the Strategic Plan taken directly from the report, as I mentioned, supports creation from the annual work plans for each committee. Committees are where the work actually happens. Right? Folks that are actually out there, boots on the ground and they provide staff, hopefully will provide the staff and board oversight. And then we'll hand off to Lisa with, you know, some of those findings. But, but again, our goal is to create the committees that will sort of advise the board and develop new strategies and new plans. But again, I\rquote ll pass it off to Lisa at this time. \par
\par
Ms. Lisa Finkelstein stated thank you, Kyle. So I\rquote m going to I\rquote m going to run through a couple of the initiatives. We had three main Initiatives in year zero as we're, we're calling it and, and share some of our early accomplishments. So first and foremost, our Ambassadors, they've been with us since mid-November, as was mentioned. And, and the statistics that they provide to us is an important benefit of the contract that we have with them. So these are just a few highlights. But of node 121,000 hours or tasks logged over the course of the time they've been here. And another, another statistic that jumps out at me would be the 900 business outreach contacts that they've made over that course of time to they really do make an effort to get into the businesses, to talk to them, to pass information from us to the businesses and then gather information from the businesses and bring it to us. Emanuel's handed me, you know, many business cards from different small business owners wanting to reach out. So it's been a really good conduit for us to the businesses. They can track a variety of interactions and including pedestrian traffic. So they're currently working with us through our board and our committees to determine what types of statistics would be useful for us to have to share with our stakeholders, with the businesses. And, and we're working on refining the type of things that the information that we gather and then can use to inform our program decisions. It's, it's really also important to note that having the Ambassadors in the downtown gives the businesses a feeling of support, and especially single operator businesses where you are by yourself, in your, in your shop or your office location all day to have that Ambassador check on you or know that they're around is, is a good feeling. And having been a single business owner, I can relate to that. So our next slide, this shows what some of our residents are saying. So not statistics, but anecdotal evidence that they are making a difference. These are some comments that were gathered from some of the residents. So you can see even in the pictures where they're, you know, the guys are interacting with some of the residents that are just sitting outside enjoying the weather or coming to play corn hole at one of our activations. But in fact, this afternoon, as we were coming out of our, our Founders Council luncheon, we spied Jim walking down the street helping a woman. He was carrying two huge bags of diapers. The handles had broken, and she was struggling to get them back to her apartment so we caught him in the act today, but it's great to see. We also have some business testimonials to. And you know, they're again, appreciating the information, but they're also benefiting from the fact that our guys are trained and, and we're all benefiting from that. So it's not that these gentlemen or these, these people are hired and put out on the streets. They, on a weekly, regular basis, receive training. So just in June, you can see on this on the screen for trainings that they are five trainings that they all receive during the month of June, encounters with people on the street, mental health awareness, extreme weather, which is hot or cold, and then the construction hazard awareness, which is really important right now with all that's going on downtown and, and safety on our info track, which if you haven't seen, you'll start to see around town, but we had it at the Community Bike Works. It's a neat, neat information trike (sp) that we can use to raise awareness for the program. So the next steps for the Ambassadors really will include, you know, continuing to work on the relationships with the local businesses, with the residents, raising the visibility of the program among the public. Most of the business owners now are aware of it and know what it is, but a lot of people, you know, that aren't downtown on a regular basis are still questioning what it is. So we want to push out some things on social media and in other ways to raise awareness. We'd like to build some staffing capacity. Jim's been working on that additional capacity in the form of a part time Ambassador, would allow them to work longer days. For instance, when we have activations at lunchtime, and then we also have an evening activation or there's a show at, at PPL, it creates a rather long day and puts them maybe over their hours for the week. So having that additional person would give them the flexibility to structure their days. And then again, evolving that performance measurement what are the key performance indicators that we need to, you know, satisfy our investors and our grant obligations? And, how can they help us to accumulate them? So the second initiative that I\rquote d like to talk about is the brand development and the marketing. As Matt's talked a little bit about the brand launch. And Kyle also mentioned it too, that it really we feel the brand reflects our identity as an urban arts and business district. It has vibrant colors, it has an edgy vibe. It's very authentic with the tagline real good times, emphasizing the real because they real really are real. And then sharing these brand elements out with our partners, our small businesses, so that they can use them in their marketing and you're starting to see that if you're on social media, that it's being utilized. Again, it raises awareness for the downtown. It unifies it. It provides a cohesiveness to the downtown that we feel is really important. We also have launched a website. It's an experiential website so it has right now six different experiences. So for somebody that's looking at coming to Allentown, perhaps for a conference, or they live nearby, but they haven't been downtown in a while, and maybe they're coming in for a show and they're figuring, you know, what else can I do? They can look at the website, pick an experience, maybe a date night or a staycation, and they can find suggestions on their itinerary where they might want to eat, where they might want to shop, where they might want to stay, and things that they would like to do here. So we are we've started with a variety of different ideas to get people thinking. But really, again, with that idea of, of increasing the dwell time that people spend here in downtown so they may come in for one event, you know, maybe a show at the Symphony, but we want them to stay and do at least two or three different things, whether it's, you know, shop in a retail store first or go for dinner or go for dessert after the show, that type of thing. So this is part of our plan to do that. We also, as was mentioned earlier, started with our social media manager July 1st. So we had been had a small presence on Instagram prior to that. But really, these are the numbers since July 1st. So you can see that there's that going from nothing, we've, we've done, you know, quite a bit in a short period of time. I don't know if any of you saw it, but just yesterday we had a TikTok video that's on a couple of our channels featuring Flowers Perez on Linden Street, and it sort of went viral. As of today, there were 13,400 views of that video. And, and the actually the TikTok followers now number 538 compared to the number 101, which was at the end of July. So, so you can really see the progression there and the stronger this gets and the more we can amplify the work that the, the businesses downtown are already doing and draw attention to them. So it's really a benefit that, that the DAA can provide to the entire district. We're continuing to monitor the reactions to the social media so that it will inform our next steps. Speaking of next steps, in terms of the brand and the marketing, we're looking at creating a very simple to use brand marketing toolkit. So packaging those assets we already have so that we have a really nice toolkit that we can share with our partners. We have created a wish list for Phase Two of the website, including an English to Spanish translation, a full blown business directory, and some other features. And we're working on a marketing campaign. We have a marketing strategy that we've reviewed that's identified for different audiences. So we have Lehigh Valley residents, we have downtown residents and workers. We have the Hispanic and Latino community that surrounds downtown. And then we have the regional event goers that are maybe coming in for a particular event that we would like to, to capture. So then the third prong of this are the activations and. And again, Matt addressed this a little bit, but you can see here in numbers in the fall we had 10 activations, so roughly 10 hours of programming that happened all at the PPL Plaza in accompanying events, various events that were there in the spring. Since we started at the beginning of April, we've had 110 hours of activation, and it's been across four locations downtown. So it's been at the PPL Center, but also at the path, the pocket park on the Arts Walk and at DLP Plaza down on the corner of Ninth. So we're, we're getting weekly Reports from our activation manager and the ambassadors, which is allowing for modifications along the way. So for instance, Lunch Break Live, which is a Music Series that happens from 12 to 1, was originally happening on a Friday. And we realized that a lot of the employees don't come downtown on Fridays to work. So we moved it over to a Thursday and it seems to be gaining traction there. Also, the Walk This Way Thursday, which is a Music Series in the pocket park that was just merely the music and people gathering and playing corn hole. And we've added a mobile bar to that. We're working with Simpatico, so they're, they're helping us again, supporting a local business, not bringing in an outside vendor. And our goal there with these activations is really that compliment. So it's meant to, you know, add vibrancy to the, the street and the public areas, engaging people, whether they want to sit and eat their lunch or they just want to enjoy the music as they walk by, you know, they feel like there's life on the streets. So we're, you know, hoping that it's encouraging our residents to come outside and look forward to it. And we know by some of our repeat visitors to these activations, but also that it encourages the workers and the event goers to stay a while or to come back again. So here too, we have next steps. We're going to maintain the Walk This Way Thursday Program, the Lunch Break Live and our Wellness Program through the through October. They've been doing well. And like I said, we've made some modifications there. We're adding a yoga on Wednesday evening. So that'll be two Wellness Programs, a Saturday Morning Zumba and, and the Wednesday evening yoga. And we're, we're looking forward to hosting a Global Marketplace Festival in the fall. We're anticipating November. This is really going to be a proof of concept for a recurring Downtown Market. But, we wanted to make it a Festival. We want to get a lot of vendors there, get a lot of attendees there, and really do some surveying. And, what do people want to see? What day of the week would they like a Market? What hours of the day, what product mix would they like, you know, fresh vegetables, prepared food, you know, all of the things. So we want to have that opportunity. We're working in partnership with Blue Zones Project to help with the surveying for the market. We really want this market to celebrate the cultural diversity. We think that's how this market will be set apart from other markets throughout the Lehigh Valley. And, so we want to look at both at the product mix, the food, the entertainment, all of that to celebrate that Cultural Diversity that's so prevalent in Allentown. We also want it to be walkable, fresh produce. We think that's important. And so we're working with some local farmers that specifically grow for Farmer's Markets and, and make it a place that downtown visit, but also employees can grab and visit and go home, you know, take home with them if they're not living downtown. So and this is where the, our ability to provide and a place for entrepreneurs or creative people to be vendors and then have an opportunity to move on through the channel, we're envisioning a shared space where they might graduate to if they've, you know, been successful as vendors and then ultimately helping them to find a space downtown that fits their needs, if that's what, what they would like to do. We're looking ahead to Center Square being finished in many ways. And when that's done, we're, we're looking forward to programming that both with music and, and hopefully the market would. That's that would be the location of the market at some point. So and then we're in the process right now of hiring a part time Event Coordinator. This person would assist me, but they would allow us to have improved coordination and communication between the event organizers, the downtown businesses, and again, complementing existing events with additional activations. So identifying where those events are and, and finding ways to support them with these additional activations. So a lot on our plate as far as the, the public space vibrancy goes, I\rquote m going to pivot into a high level view of the revenue and expenses. I\rquote m going to start with expenses and look at our year zero, 2020 five, 26 actuals compared to our 2026-27 budget. And, and here you can see in the formative year, we had very high administrative costs, really due mostly to the United Way Contract. They were acting as our incubator. So there was a monthly fee for that contract that ended in May. So we are we no longer have that expense and then of course, there were additional startup costs associated with, you know, forming the organization itself. But even so, 64% of the dollars spent went directly to the Programs. So we feel good about that.  In, in year one, this current year, the budget calls for a significant reduction in the administrative costs. And then the program, the dollar spent on the programs jumps to 81% of our budget. So we really feel like this shows that we are moving in the right direction in terms of being fiscally responsible. When I move over to the revenue side in year zero, the original year, you can see that the revenue was really evenly spread, spread among the city, other public sources and private dollars in year one. That really changes the city funds would represent 24%, rather than 34% of the total, and due in part to the pie getting bigger. And the pie got bigger because of the NPP contributors. So that program would be a game changer for us.  It would give us a stable revenue stream for the next six years. We have nine contributors, for a total of $675,000 a year, but none of that is certain at this point so if, if you look at the, the next slide is shows the same revenue pie for the current year, but the gray spaces are not confirmed. They are projected. So you can see that, you know, it's quite a lot of it. And we would have to adjust the budget. If any of this does not come through. So while we expect that the remaining private dollars will definitely be secured, you can just see on this Chart how critical the, the city funding is as an anchor for the rest of the budget. So and you know, Matt brought this up as a public/private partnership, which is so critical to the success of this organization that it remains that way, that it is really, truly, you know, a blend of all of, of these areas. Interview Process:

1.  Candidates were chosen at random and will be interviewed as follows:
Evette D'Amore
Jasmine Salgado
Patrick Palmer

2.  Candidate Presentation – 10 Minutes
Based on your professional experience and qualifications, please explain why you would be a strong City Controller and how your experience would bring value to the City.

3.   Closing Statement – 2 Minutes
Why should City Council appoint you as City Controller?

4.   Following the interviews, each Councilperson will complete and sign a ballot indicating their choice for City Controller. The City Clerk will read the selected candidate from each ballot aloud. The voting process will continue until a candidate receives a majority of votes.

4. Each Councilperson can ask one follow up question to each candidate and the candidate has two minutes to reply. 

5. Public Comment will be taken before Council makes the choice on the first ballot. 

COUNCIL RULES - RULE XX - FILLING OF VACANCIES - COUNCIL, CONTROLLER AND MAYOR
     Vacancies shall be filled according to the requirements of the charter – sections 207, 304 and 405. When a vacancy occurs in the office of Council, Controller or the Mayor, City Council shall immediately advertise the vacancy in a local newspaper, on the City’s website and notify the political party of the person who left office that Council will be accepting applications to fill the vacant position.  Applications shall consist of a resume and a statement stating the reasons the applicant will bring value to the City as a Councilperson, Mayor or City Controller. Applications shall be received no later than fourteen days after the effective date of the vacancy. 
              The applications shall be reviewed by the President or Acting President of Council to make sure the applicant is qualified pursuant to the charter and applicable state law. The replacement must be a qualified voter of the same party as the person vacating the seat at least 30 days prior to the vacancy. After review, Council shall have a public meeting to review the resumes and statements of the applicants and interview each of the candidates. The candidates shall be chosen in a random fashion for interviews.
              After the interviews, Council shall vote on the candidates to fill the vacancy at a public meeting. Each councilperson will fill out and sign a ballot indicating their choice to fill the position. The ballots shall be given to the City Clerk who shall read aloud the name of the candidate selected by each councilperson. The process continues until a candidate earns a majority of votes. (26631 10/7/92; 25142 2/2/83; 26631 10/7/92; 28809 11/2/2011; 29619 3/14/2018)

SECTION 405. Vacancy.
A.  If the office of the City Controller becomes vacant for any reason, Council shall appoint an interim City Controller, of the same political party, who shall serve until the next Municipal Election.
B.   A vacancy in the office of the City Controller shall be filled at the next Municipal Election, in the manner provided by law. The person elected shall hold the qualifications for the office of the City Controller and shall serve the remaining portion of the vacated term.

Before we start, I just want to take a some moment, a moment here to explain where we are in the process of filling this vacancy in the office of City Controller. How we got here and what happens next? First, the City Controller plays a vital role in Allentown government.  The Controller provides independent financial oversight of city finances, reviews expenditures across city government, reviews the annual budget, and may make recommendations to the mayor and City Council.  They attend Council meetings and perform audits, among other responsibilities.  Following the vacancy in the Controller's office, City Council began the appointment process required under the Home Rule Charter.  Council publicly advertised a vacancy in the newspaper, city website, LinkedIn, through a Press Release, Social media at Council meetings and Indeed.  Applicants were required to submit a resume and a statement explaining the value they would bring as a City Controller.  Because the previous Controller, Mr. Jeff Glazier, was a democrat. The Home Rule Charter and Council Rules require the person appointed to fill the vacancy to be a qualified voter and a member of the same political party. We also sent a letter to the local democratic party informing them of the Vacancy.  After the application period closed, Council reviewed the applicants and scheduled a Public meeting to interview qualified candidates.  The intent throughout this process has been to conduct the interviews and appointment publicly, so residents can hear directly from the candidates and understand Council's decision.  Due to scheduling conflicts, our originally scheduled meeting of July 2 was postponed to today.  In the meantime, we continue to take resumes until Monday, August 20.  We received over 50 resumes and after a thorough review by Council staff, we're down to three candidates.  We're now approaching the end of our process. Tonight, we will ask the candidates to go through an interview with City Council, and after that we will proceed to a vote.   Once an appointment is made, that individual will serve as Interim City Controller until the end of 2027.   He stated okay, we'll start the meeting. Mr. Hanlon, can you do a roll call, please? \par
\par
Mr. Michael Hanlon read the Roll Call and stated he was waiting for Ms. Affa.  \par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated okay, keep us posted on that. We'll start to move this along so regarding interview process, candidates were chosen at random by Council staff and will be interviewed as follows:  First, Ms. Yvette D'Amore; second, Jasmine, Ms. Jasmine Salgado; and third, Mr. Patrick Palmer.  Each candidate will have a presentation of 10 minutes to let us know your  professional experience and qualifications and explain why you would be a strong City Controller and how your experience would bring value to the city.  You also have a closing statement of two minutes of why City Council should appoint you as a City Controller.  My colleagues will have an opportunity for one follow up question for each candidate.
