So last year, my colleagues and I, seven nothing vote authorized an increase of a half percent to the Deed Transfer Tax for Real Estate transactions in the city of Allentown. This increase would not affect any existing homeowners or seniors and was focused on improving housing conditions citywide, much of which has been neglected for years due to budget concerns. This additional revenue was all pointed to a housing fund within our city department. Based on previous years data, the estimate was approximately 2.3 million a year. As of June 30th of this year, the Housing Fund has received $1,080,000. My legislation also calls for an Annual Action Plan, which was a public meeting to discuss how best to utilize housing fund dollars for housing initiatives throughout the city. So we met with Councilperson Frank Pettibone. He's from Easton, and they passed a Workforce Housing piece of legislation recently. Bill 61    
Amending the 2026 Risk Fund by transferring Six Million Five Hundred Thousand ($6,500,000) Dollars from the General Fund unappropriated balance to the Risk Fund for the payment of healthcare claims, drug prescription benefits, and other employee medical costs for the remainder of the year, as well as for insurance costs, and property and auto losses. Amounts for healthcare claims are significantly higher this year and certain losses have been experienced at rates higher than expected.

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\sa160\sl276\slmult1\qj\kerning2\f0\fs20 Mr. Santo Napoli stated yeah, okay, so we're going to kick off this meeting. It's a Special Meeting for Wednesday, September 9th, 2026. Can you do the Roll Call, please, Ms. Ortega. \par
Amending Part 1 - Administrative Legislation, Chapter 75 - Pensions and Retirement, Article III - Police Pension Fund, by adding a new Section 75-53 \ldblquote Limited Deferred Retirement Option Plan\rdblquote . \par
Ms. Genesis Ortega stated that Ms. Mota cannot make it today. \par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated okay, thank you. So, tonight's Special Meeting we have a topic regarding the Pension Reform Bill to DROP at the request of the FOP, this meeting was scheduled to share details and take potential questions from his colleagues and the public. He stated that they haven't and have the president our FOP president, Mr. Chris Matthews, and thank you for joining and Frank Kane, our Managing Director; and stated that he will pass it on to you and the presentation is all yours. \par
Sergeant Chris Matthews stated yeah, thank you very much so thank you all again. It's nice to see you all from the last time we were here, just to there were a bunch of questions that were brought up in the last meeting as far as stats and statistics related to our hiring, our staffing. While I won't go into specific numbers and details about that, I will say that the officers that retired in 2025, we still have not replaced them so we have had other officers retire already in 2026, and we again, still have not replaced them either. So the purpose of the DROP is again, to slow the number of officers that are separating from the city while we ramp up recruiting efforts to be able to backfill the already open spots while not creating additional existing open spots. And additionally, this is the Referendum for Amending the Pension Ordinance for City Council is simply to reflect the already signed Agreement between the mayor and the FOP currently. \par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated okay.\par
Mr. Frank Kane stated so maybe he could wait and stated so broadly he thinks you all know this, but if you don't, you know, the DROP is a Program. It's a Deferred Retirement Program. The point of the thing is to get people to stay. We're having and it's a very difficult time to recruit new police officers. For whatever reason, we're not experiencing much success, nor is any department really anywhere experiencing success in recruiting police officers so what we have entered into an Agreement to do, as many other municipalities have is when a Police Officer hits their retirement rather than retire, they leave, you know, they leave the Pension Program portion of the city, right and so then they receive the city, pays out, continues to pay out their pension payments, but into another pot of money, and then that pot of money accumulates over five years and then when they when they exit, they take that money with them, you know, and we retain the interest our pension and thinks the assumption is what is the DROP gives you 4.5, 5.5 the drop on the money. \par
Mr. Christopher Matthews stated so the money stays in the Pension Fund. It doesn't go into a separate account. It simply dog eared for when the officer separates so whatever remaining interest up until 4.5% is what the officers would get at time of separation. Any remaining interest stays in the Pension Fund.  \par
Mr. Frank Kane stated right, so all of the interest that accrues, he means, this could come close to being cost neutral, depending on how investments go and how, you know, and how the market goes and how our, our, our, you know, how our payouts go. So really the way to look at it is it's a, it is a tool to, you know, it's for operations, it's for operational continuity. We, if we were to experience a mass retirement of 20 or 30 officers at the end of the year, it would be very difficult for, for the department to function and to provide all the services that people in Allentown expect. So that's why the mayor has entered into this Agreement. \par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated okay. He asked is any other or anything else before he takes some questions? \par
Sergeant Christopher Matthews stated no, he is open to any questions. Thank you. \par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated okay, any questions from his colleagues regarding the DROP and since the last meeting, anything? He sated okay. He means, he can say the one, the one issue he has continued to hear is not knowing what this will cost because it's a it's a concern, you know, from a budget standpoint, you know, you're, we're doing something when, when you build a, a Capital Project, you know, what it's going to cost and how that's amortized over 10 years, 20 years. This it's, it's, he thinks is one of the concerns he heard is how much is it? And I don't know if there's an answer to that, but it's hard. It's hard to justify it. \par
Sergeant Christopher Matthews stated that he will say that in his opinion, the cost of doing the DROP is significantly much less than it will be the cost of not doing the DROP the way it is supposed to be done. \par
Ms. Candida Affa stated say that again.\par
Sergeant Christopher Matthews stated okay. And that's and that's the cost of doing the DROP will be significantly less than the cost of if the DROP is not done the way it's supposed to be implemented, or if it's not done at all. He stated that is simply for the fact that we're going to have officers that are, are shift overtime already is up this already, this time in 2026, it is significantly higher than it was in 2025. That's because we have shift staffing issues already as they are. And again, this isn't for overtime related to Special Events or any type of, you know, if an officer has a late call, the numbers that I'm referring to are shifts, staffing numbers so if an officer is calls out sick or there's a vacancy due to any other trainings or any other type of shift staffing issue, we have a minimum number of officers that we maintain on patrol. That's the number that I'm referring to, and those are the shifts that are going to be paid out in overtime to be to continue to offer the same basic patrol services that we offer. And that's not including all of our investigative units, as well as the other specialty community outreach units that were already starting to see shortages in with the number, with the number having dropped from 2025 and that which we still haven't recovered from. \par
Mr. Frank Kane stated and if I can give you some other numbers. So we are reimbursed for each police officer, $12,500 for their Pension. So for when a person leaves the Pension Plan as an active duty police officer, let's say we no longer receive that $12,500. So for every person that enters the drop, we will not we will not receive that $12,500, right and their pension will then, you know, technically whether it'll be, you know, it'll be earmarked as, as, as a different pot of money to stay in the Pension, but technically that's, that's money that we would be paying out anyway too so he doesn't think they can really count that money as a loss. The loss is $12,500. But you know, the idea is then that we would hire other officers that would then pay into the, you know, in the time that these that these officers remained, we would then have more time to hire other recruits that would come in and that would pay into the pension fund and, you know, we would keep it solvent and would keep it growing. So it's really the $12,500 that we that we lose from the state. \par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated okay.  Thank you, Mr. Pungo. Go ahead. \par
Mr. Cristian Pungo stated absolutely. So I appreciate you guys. You know, between last meeting and this meeting, this program is touted as, you know, for the benefit of recruiting. And I know we kind of alluded to that there was some questions about that last time around. It seems like, and I think we mentioned some similar concerns at the beginning at our last meeting, just the idea of if it's a challenging environment now to hire what, you know, can we guarantee that some of these folks won't already retire? Maybe we can for some, maybe we can't, for others can we guarantee we will hire? I don't know that we necessarily can. Maybe we will increase our chances. But I guess my other part of it is if right now we're seeing a crunch and it's not just us and it's, you know, a wide crunch around, you know, different municipalities all around. Maybe this is an option, but is there any reason why it couldn't be, you know, a temporary option where if we're saying this is something that we're seeing now and it's in, you know, we want to help combat that. But, you know, I think there's at least the way that when I kind of go through the numbers and I understand it, I feel like, you know, there is a recurring cost as the program continues and as we do this and we talked about some of the, you know, potential other long term effects of, you know, what does transition planning look like? Do we have officers who stay maybe in their position? And then it limits some of the other folks who could kind of climb up the ranks. I'm not saying that's what's going to happen. I'm just saying if these are possibilities, you know, is it necessarily the tool that we want to keep for the long term versus, you know, to, you know, fill in a moment where we're seeing a struggle? \par
Mr. Frank Kane stated that I understand, I mean, from the administration's perspective and then I'll let Sergeant Matthews give the FOP perspective. But where we are right now is we have a we have a negotiated Agreement between the administration and the FOP. It's been it goes through process to be voted by the membership there and this is the document that we have to bring before you. And I don't think I don't know if there would be a process to amend it.  I think it's just the Agreement is in its final form. \line\par
Sergeant Christopher Matthews stated that the agreement is in its final form, and part of the issue that you run into is if you put an end date on the DROP, would you end up having is a. Right now we're dealing with the mass exodus that we and that the department felt in 2005, where our numbers dropped significantly, much lower than they are right now. To combat that, the department ramped up hiring and hired a large number of officers in 2006. Because of that, 20 years later, 2026, we now have a large number of officers who are ready to retire. If we do a temporary DROP, what that will do is, one, it will only benefit if we were even willing to open up the terms which were not right now. But if that were an option, what that would do is essentially take this large number of officers that can retire, that entered into the drop and build a larger number of officers that can all leave at the same time then the year that the DROP expires, if that makes sense. It does. \par
Mr. Cristian Pungo stated it does and guesses he is also curious that the same phenomenon happens now with the DROP. I believe it's over five years now. So even if the drop exists, doesn't that just kind of shift that time horizon? Five years and an issue that we're seeing in 2026 becomes a 2031 issue.   \par
Sergeant Christopher Matthews stated yes and no because what it does is it buys us time to ramp up our recruiting efforts and again, be able to and also use the DROP as a recruitment tool. It also gives officers the freedom entering into the DROP does not lock you in for a full five years or 60 months. Once you're in, you can do as much or as little of that time as you'd like in the DROP. So what it does is it spreads, it spreads it out a little bit. And we're not having these large numbers of mass exoduses.\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated okay. Thank you. \par
Sergeant Christopher Matthews stated you're welcome. \par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated okay, Ms. Affa.\par
Ms. Candida Affa stated she thinks you can appreciate the fact that we have to vote on something that we don't have true numbers on. We can't look at figures and think, well, if we do this, it's an advantage or disadvantage because of the money. We don't have any true figures on things. We don't know if another plan as like I'm a proponent of recruiting more, using the money to get more police officers out there. So if we don't have true figures and numbers to compare and make a decision on, it's very difficult for us to say, well, well, it could be this much or it could be that much or if we have a different plan in mind, we might all decide that, that we have a different plan or we don't have a different plan, but another plan can come up that will be more advantage to the city with more patrolmen and so on and so forth. It makes us it's difficult if we don't have these true figures, and we've been asking for it for like forever, but you can't come up with any of them. How much it's really going to cost with the DROP? You don't know. And we have to make a decision on we don't know. \par
Sergeant Christopher Matthews stated so if I may. They will use, we'll use 2026, for example, the officers that are that are eligible to leave at the end of this year, if those officers leave, they're gone. The money the Pension Fund ceases to get the state funding that we would get for those officers. The Pension Fund loses the money out of the Pension Fund on a on a bi weekly basis and all the while we are we're in the position where we are hiring overtime or stripping down various units throughout the department, reducing the services that are offered to the public while we try to hire those officers. And again, even when we hire officers, it's we have the Academy, which is a 28 week program. We have our field training program, which also takes a couple months. So it's not an instant fix to, to just hire all these officers the entire time. The city will incur those costs. \par
Ms. Candida Affa stated but if I may interrupt you a minute, Mr. Pungo's idea would then be something to think about.  We could then if it's five years or whatever, we could see the plan working. But for forever.  It's exactly what you're talking about. We'll see the plan. We'll see how it's working. We'll see how much money it costs. We can understand and see everything that we see the plan. But for us to vote like a forever thing, it's I mean.\par
Mr. Frank Kane stated that at one point that he would like to make is that it's a projection. Like, like all budgeting is a projection.  Nobody really knows what your, what your healthcare costs are going to be next year. We just did a whole, we just did a whole, a whole committee on. We, we don't we don't know. We can guess. We have numbers. We, you know, we, we project that we're going to spend $30,000 per employee. But, you know, you don't really know. And the same thing, we don't really know how many people are going to go into the DROP. We don't know the money we're going to. We have an Actuarial Study which you've which you've seen and you've seen those projections, but all budgeting is really just projections. There's really no way to know. At the end of the day.\par
Ms. Candida Affa stated that five year plan would be much better. She thinks we have a we have we. It's not that's not the agreement we have is the is the issue today. \par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated okay. Any other questions or comments from colleagues? Okay. Any questions from the public? Welcome. \par
Mr. Cristian Pungo stated push button. This one. \par
Ms. Barbara Redmond stated good evening, my name is Barbara Redmond with Improving Lives and I agree with Ms.Affa. You need to have some kind of plan. How can you go out there and have the taxpayers pay for something they don't know what they're paying for? If you have a plan, it sounds good, but you need to be in paper writing so everybody can see it and understand what's going on. \par
Thank you. \par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated thank you. Any other comments from the public? Okay. He stated that he did put together a statement just to make sure he covered everything, but at this point, I just want to thank you for answering some questions from council. On behalf of City Council, I want to thank everyone who did provide information, participated in discussion, public safety and supporting our police officers are extremely important to us, and I want to encourage continued conversations about how we can strengthen the department and address the staffing needs. I also want to remind everyone that earlier this summer, City Council approved the hiring of Maher Duessel to conduct a financial analysis of the city's financial position and provide council with additional information to make informed financial decisions. The firm is preparing a five year financial projection that will give us greater context, as we consider significant financial commitments, and how those decisions could affect the city budget in the years ahead these aren't easy decisions, and they're not decisions that take lightly. Our responsibility is to do our due diligence and make sure we're making decisions that are in the best interest of our residents, while also supporting our city workforce is expected to deliver its financial projections by mid-October. And with that in mind, I hope everyone will respect council's decision to pause consideration of the draft program until we have an opportunity to receive and review that analysis. In the meantime, I encourage the administration, the fop and my colleagues to continue discussions about other ways we can address apd staffing challenges. I would like us to look. I would like us to look more closely at how we can improve recruitment and develop incentives that help us attract and retain officers. Ultimately, we need to be thinking beyond the immediate staffing challenge. We don't want to find ourselves having the same conversations five years from now. My colleague Councilwoman Affa, who chairs the Public Safety Committee, has already expressed interest in considering and evaluating long term solutions. She's extremely supportive of Public Safety. I know she will help lead that conversation. So again, thank you all. We'll pick up this conversation after Council has had a chance to consider this Program in the context of the five year financial projection and the 2027 budget process. So thank you, FOP president\par
Sergeant Christopher Matthews stated if I may, I would strongly urge and request that city council vote on this pension ordinance referendum sooner rather than later, please. This contract was signed by the administration, the mayor, back in February, and my members have waited very patiently since February of this past year to for this for the administration to get this part of the this mandatory function resolved, as it's the mayor's responsibility to execute all contracts and written obligations of the city. That's what this is. And waiting until mid-October puts the officers who would be retiring at the end of the year. And with certain timelines that are laid out in our contract, as well as with the city, we'll put them in a very tight bind. As far as, you know, the employees making the decision of what they're going to be doing in the new year. So I would strongly urge city council to take the information that they have at hand and vote on the at the next possible meeting. \par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated okay. Well, thank you for that. I'm unfortunately, I have to respectfully push back. And we hired a firm to help us with budget planning and help us for the next five years, make sure we have an obligation to our residents to make sure our budget is appropriately funded and used. And that's why we paused Capital Projects. We. We paused the. We didn't. The DROP is part of it, and we really want to understand where we're going before we make these decisions that make. That could have serious impacts on our residents from a budget standpoint over the next few years. And for us to make a decision like this prior to getting that information, I think would be not very thoughtful or prudent to our residents who are counting on us to make the best decisions possible for our budget. So while I do respect and appreciate where you're coming from, I sincerely mean that. I hope you respect where we're coming from, what we're trying to figure out where we're going, not just for 2027, but for the years after in these really important decisions on Capital Projects and a Pension Reform Bill such as the draft and my colleagues, I've pulled them and they all feel the same way. So I, I, I'm speaking on behalf of council, not myself, that they're all waiting for this, this, this report, you know, in mid October to help guide us prudently, you know, into the budget process and over the next few years. \par
Sergeant Christopher Matthews stated that he understand that. However, this is a negotiated benefit that has already been entered into by the city with employees, the members of the FOP that are actively working. This is not a Capital Project. This is a negotiated benefit that's already been signed and entered into with the city. And this is a necessary function, a mandatory function of City Council to amend this. This is no different than the Act 47 benefit that was introduced and spoken about for two minutes at the City Council, two City Council meetings ago and voted on. That was also negotiated benefit that was entered into with this between the city and the FOP. This is no different. \par
\f1 Mr. Santo Napoli stated that his colleagues find it very different, and I'm sorry that it's unfortunate that we're being put in this position.  But and ultimately, that's why we're waiting to hear back from Maher Duessel.  And that's really our intent is to follow that advice.  And if we make decisions before we get that advice, I don't think I, I know a lot of residents would not look favorably on that.  I think they're counting on us to make the best decision.  So we're waiting for that Report.  And I'm sorry that it doesn't it doesn't match up with you with your timeline.  I'm sorry that it doesn't work out like that.  But we're focused on our budget and our next five years.  And this Report  And this Report coming out October 15th is crucial for us.  So that's why we all feel like that.  So again, I'm sorry.  Nothing Just being respectful.\par
Sergeant Christopher Matthews stated that you don't need to apologize to me. The 30 plus officers that now need to wait until the middle of October for this to a decision to even be thought about being made and trying to figure out how they're going to be planning the rest of their lives. After doing over 20 years of service to the city. Those are the people that should be apologized to.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated okay. All right. Well, that being said, that wraps up our meeting.\f0\fs24\par
}

\par

\par

\par

\par

Courtesy of the Floor Rules and Privileges
•	Our complete set of council rules are posted online and also stapled to the meeting agendas located on the back table of council chambers.  
•	Council Rules have established a three-minute time limit for speakers.
•	Speakers are asked to state their name for the record.
•	Speakers shall direct their comments to the President of Council, rather than to individual Council members, Council staff, members of the City’s Administration, or members of the public.
•	During this public meeting, speakers are expected to treat all individuals with dignity and respect. Comments that demean, harass, threaten, or discriminate against an individual or group based on characteristics such as race, color, ethnicity, national origin, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, disability, age, or other protected status are not appropriate during public comment.
•	Speakers must follow the direction of the Council President and refrain from interrupting or disrupting the meeting. Failure to comply may result in the speaker forfeiting the remainder of their time at the podium and being asked to return to their seat. \par

\par
Mr. Jeremy Binder stated thank you, President Napoli. I just want to make a couple of quick comments on this for Council members here. So I began this process back in March of 2026 to review how surveillance is being handled within the city limits. I met with the mayor and the Chief of Police at the time about trying to obtain information about what Flock safety systems were being deployed in Allentown and who we were sharing data with. My goal in this process, my goal trajectory in this process has been to create some sort of Ordinance for public oversight of surveillance technologies, and then to have that reference, a surveillance use policy, which would live, would be a living document within the administrative handbook, outlining the criteria and guardrails that departments within the city would adhere to related to anything with surveillance. I recommended to the city to explore obtaining information from IPVM so they could help navigate this process. I currently just for. For full transparency, I subscribe to IPVM in my professional role as a service. This organization, this organization focuses on doing independent reviews in the surveillance industry. That is their sole focus. They're not a they're not funded through any manufacturers or like that. And they for, for the surveillance industry provide a very non or very unbiased technical approach to it. But in this case, if this passes, would be focusing on how the city can understand what it is that we've deployed, what are the risks that are out there, and how we can properly craft some policy going forward? There has been a lot of feedback from the public. I know some people have brought this up for a year or two now at this point, and I think this is a good next step in creating that, that, that policy for us to be able to look at. And then for all of us to be able to evaluate, I\rquote d encourage everyone to, to move this forward. But I do want to make sure it's very clear this is coming out of Council's budget. I think it's important that since the since the public has come to us and said, hey, we're interested in this, that, you know, we're taking this initiative to try and come up with a good policy. And that's where the funding would come from. So I just wanted to I know there was a little long there, but make sure it was very clear what the reason was for this, why it was Single Sourced. I'm a big fan of their work, but why waste a $10,000 when the hackers of the world will do it for free? Thank you. \par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated okay. Any other questions or comments from the public on R111.\par
\par
Mr. Frank Kane stated yeah, I, if I can.\par
\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated go ahead. \par
\par
Mr. Frank Kane stated so, you know, when we look, this is one of the first issues that I bumped into when I, when I came here in April and our Police Department uses Flock Technology and solves crimes because of Flock Technology, but we are not comfortable as a, you know, as an administration. And when we looked into this, you know, in terms of the procurement, when we looked into companies that provide this service, lots of companies will tell you that they'll, that they will audit your use of a technology. Mr. Santo Napoli stated okay, Mr. Binder, go ahead. \par

Council Rules have established a three minute time limit for speakers. Speakers are asked to state their name for the record. Speakers shall direct their comments to the president Council rather than to individual Council members, Council staff, members of the city's administration or members of the public. During this meeting, public speakers are expected to treat all individuals with dignity and respect. Comments that demean, harass, threaten or discriminate against an individual or group based on characteristics such as race, color, ethnicity, national origin, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, disability, age, or other protected status are not appropriate during public comment. \par

agenda_items.title:
Courtesy of the Floor Rules and Privileges
•	Our complete set of council rules are posted online and also stapled to the meeting agendas located on the back table of council chambers.  
•	Council Rules have established a three-minute time limit for speakers.
•	Speakers are asked to state their name for the record.
•	Speakers shall direct their comments to the President of Council, rather than to individual Council members, Council staff, members of the City’s Administration, or members of the public.
•	During this public meeting, speakers are expected to treat all individuals with dignity and respect. Comments that demean, harass, threaten, or discriminate against an individual or group based on characteristics such as race, color, ethnicity, national origin, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, disability, age, or other protected status are not appropriate during public comment.
•	Speakers must follow the direction of the Council President and refrain from interrupting or disrupting the meeting. Failure to comply may result in the speaker forfeiting the remainder of their time at the podium and being asked to return to their seat.  Continued interruption of the meeting may result in the speaker being removed from council chambers.
Contract Approvals: The general idea for approving contracts is that the council acknowledges that proper procurement procedures were followed pursuant to the city code.

Bill 74
Amending the 2026 Capital Fund Budget to provide for an increase of Six Hundred Thousand Dollars ($600,000.00) to fund the approved Public Works capital project to replace the salt shed as part of the 2026 Capital borrowing. Increasing our storage capacity is important for both operational and financial reasons. It is common for other townships, municipalities, and the state to experience delays or shortages in salt deliveries during the winter season. When this occurs, we are often forced to purchase salt at significantly higher prices simply to maintain our ability to respond to winter storms and keep our roads safe. Doubling our salt storage capacity would allow us to purchase the majority of our salt at the beginning of the season at the contracted rate, rather than having to compete with surrounding townships and municipalities for limited supplies later in the season. This would provide greater reliability during winter storms while also helping to control costs and avoid potentially significant emergency purchases.

Courtesy of the Floor
Courtesy of the Floor Rules and Privileges
•	Our complete set of council rules are posted online and stapled to the meeting agendas located on the back table of council chambers.  
•	Council Rules have established a three-minute time limit for speakers.
•	Speakers are asked to state their name for the record.
•	Speakers shall direct their comments to the President of Council, rather than to individual Council members, Council staff, members of the City’s Administration, or members of the public.
•	During this public meeting, speakers are expected to treat all individuals with dignity and respect. Comments that demean, harass, threaten, or discriminate against an individual or group based on characteristics such as race, color, ethnicity, national origin, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, disability, age, or other protected status are not appropriate during public comment.
•	Speakers must follow the direction of the Council President and refrain from interrupting or disrupting the meeting. Failure to comply may result in the speaker forfeiting the remainder of their time at the podium and being asked to return to their seat.  Continued interruption of the meeting may result in the speaker being removed from council chambers

agenda_items.title:
Bill 74
Amending the 2026 Capital Fund Budget to provide for an increase of Six Hundred Thousand Dollars ($600,000.00) to fund the approved Public Works capital project to replace the salt shed as part of the 2026 Capital borrowing. Increasing our storage capacity is important for both operational and financial reasons. It is common for other townships, municipalities, and the state to experience delays or shortages in salt deliveries during the winter season. When this occurs, we are often forced to purchase salt at significantly higher prices simply to maintain our ability to respond to winter storms and keep our roads safe. Doubling our salt storage capacity would allow us to purchase the majority of our salt at the beginning of the season at the contracted rate, rather than having to compete with surrounding townships and municipalities for limited supplies later in the season. This would provide greater reliability during winter storms while also helping to control costs and avoid potentially significant emergency purchases.

It is a lot of time and, and, and the appreciation goes out to both the people on the boards and all of the people who applied to be filling those positions.   So, so please don't, you know, take any of this dialog as something that's against you specifically.  But I think from an ethics perspective, since there's been some concerns raised, it seems like it makes the most sense to at least get advice and if it comes back and says it's good from a, from a position of, of your employer as well as from a position of anything else related to the city, then great. And, then we would untable that once that opinion is received, Is that a fair way of doing it? \par

Attorney Maria Montero stated yes.\par

Mr. Jeremy Binder stated that would be my Motion. And the second? \par

Ms. Ce Ce Gerlach stated I will second. Can I ask for a point of clarification? Would that ethical body be the Sate Ethics Board or is there another ethical body? \par

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\sa160\sl276\slmult1\kerning2\f0\fs22 Controller's Report: the Controller has submitted a Report. (Accounts Payable Weekly Check Review for the Check Period End Date: (08/29 - 10/02/202)\par
\f1\fs24\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated next up is a Controller's Report. Ms. Salgado. \par
\par
Mr. Jasmine Salgado stated I want to make sure I'm speaking loud enough.  Okay. Thank you for the feedback last time.  Good evening, Council. The, the Controller's office completed a review of city expenditures and identified six areas of concern.  I want to briefly highlight our findings, the department's responses, and where we see opportunities for improvement.  First, incorrect payment amounts. We identified a garage payment of $1,354.09 for an invoice totaling $137.31, resulting in a potential overpayment of $1,216.78.  The check was requested to be voided and reissued for the correct amount.  This highlights the importance of verifying invoice amounts before payments are issued.  Second incorrect expense account we identified approximately $40,000 in expenses that were incorrectly classified between Health and Risk.  Both departments submitted correcting journal entries. However, accurate account coding is essential because it directly impacts how we monitor departmental spending and budget balances. Third mileage reimbursement documentation a Parks and Recreation reimbursement of $72.35 contained incorrect odometer readings. The department is working with administration on alternative documentation requirements.   Our recommendation is to ensure that any alternatives still provide sufficient verification before reimbursements are approved.  Four, travel expense reporting. We identified a Planning Travel Expense Report submitted 11 working days after travel despite a five day requirement.  Finance then took an additional 54 working days to review it.  Both departments were notified and finance acknowledged the oversight.  This demonstrates the need for clear processing deadlines and accountability on both sides.  Fifth, ultimately, invoice payments. This is an area I particularly want to highlight.  We identified 12 invoices across six departments with payment delays.  The reasons varied, including missing documentation, overlooked invoices, vendor communication issues, and Contract Change Orders. Currently, the city does not have a standardized time frame for invoices to move through Munis.  Invoices from receipt or delays.  Oh, was that me? Okay, that was kind of cool. All right, let me see.  I believe establishing clear timelines and responsibilities would improve efficiency, reduce unnecessary delays, and strengthen our vendor relationships. Finally, missing documentation in Munis.  We identified nine instances across five departments where required supporting documentation was not attached. The departments were notified and the documentation was subsequently scanned.   However, supporting documentation should be available at the time of review and approval not added after an issue is identified.  In closing, I want to acknowledge the departments for responding to these findings and taking corrective action, but I also want to emphasize that correcting an individual error is not necessarily the same as correcting the process that allowed it to happen.  Moving forward, I would like our office to focus on strengthening internal controls, improving consistency across departments, and following up to ensure corrective measures are working.  So thank you. \par
\par
\f0\fs22 Mayor: no submission.  \par
\f1\fs24\par
Mr. Santo Napoli stated okay. Thank you for that report.   And it looks like I don't have a Report from you this evening. \f0\fs22\par
\pard\cf1\kerning0\f2\fs24\par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\sa160\sl276\slmult1\kerning2\f0\fs24 Mr. Santo Napoli stated  Okay. Thank you and so tonight we're going to focus on Parks and Recreation for this meeting. So I'm going to hand this off to my colleague Chair, Natalie Santos, and who Chairs Parks and Recreation, and to work with the administration on the budget conversation. So take it away. \par
\par
Ms. Natalie Santos stated thank you. Welcome, everybody, to the Parks and Recreation Budget meeting. We have a couple of Bills to discuss. The first one up is Bill 83 or did you want to start? I think you had a presentation as well. However you want to do it, \par
\par
Ms. Mandy Tolino stated we can do this first. That's totally fine. \par
\par
Ms. Natalie Santos stated okay. Are you you're off. There you go. \par
\par
Ms. Mandy Tolino stated the Bill for, Bill 83 is to update the legislation to reflect the existing name of the dog park. So it's now the Judge Memorial Dog Park. So we're just updating the Code to match that. And then another important piece is that currently the key fob system is not functioning. And in order to keep it functioning, it would require significant investment. So we're proposing to remove the use of the key fobs and update the ordinance rules so that it's still the expectation that all dogs are vaccinated and required to have all their licensing, but it just wouldn't be regulated through Parks and Recreation and record keeping as well, is right now kept through the Department of Parks and Rec and it's a lot of administrative work for us to        excuse me. Keep up with all the dogs that have access to the dog park. So we are suggesting to update the legislation to remove the requirement that anyone to access the dog park needs a key fob. Thank you. \par
\par
Ms. Natalie Santos stated any comments from my colleagues on this one? \par
\par
Ms. Candida Affa stated I have some questions. How are you going to regulate dogs that are vaccinated and so on and so forth? I understand the reason we had the fob was because people were leaving the dogs and then going shopping and a lot of different things. How are and is still named Judge, right? \par
\par
Ms. Mandy Tolino stated yes. We're not changing the name. We're just change that. No, no, no, we the sign says Judge, and we're just updating the Code to reflect what the so it's up to date based on what we renamed it to, so that's kind of just a housekeeping type item. Most dog parks are, the Ordinance supports. It's the responsibility of the dog owner. So you, if you're in the city of Allentown, you have a dog and they regulate it through Animal Control as well. So you have to have licenses and vaccinations and things like that. So that expectation doesn't change. It just takes the burden of record keeping off of the Parks and Rec department. \par
\par
Ms. Candida Affa stated yeah. But my point is, if it's not the gates open to anybody, I could bring my dog. You wouldn't know if it's vaccinated or not. That's the problem with the fob prevented that and in order to get the fob, you had to have proof correct that, that the dogs were vaccinated and able to go in there. But, without the fob, the gates are open and anybody can bring their dog in and you can't. There's no way you can possibly track dogs that, that are in there that are vaccinated or not. \par
\par
Ms. Mandy Tolino stated so it is a lot of dogs and it's a lot of administrative burden for the Parks team to keep track of all those dogs and all those vaccinations. So I think that to put that responsibility on the dog owner makes more sense and that's how most dog parks are run. It's at your own risk. If you're going to bring your dog to a dog park, then it's you're assuming that the other people there are responsible dog owners as well. So that's the expectation working.\par
\par
Ms. Candida Affa asked why isn't the key fob working.  Is it a gate or.\par
\par
Ms. Mandy Tolino stated it's not the gate? It's something to do with the actual like system. So we'd have to replace the whole system. \par
\par
Ms. Candida Affa stated sorry, I didn't hear you, what.\par
\par
Ms. Mandy Tolino stated the system like the whatever mechanism that the fob communicates with in order to open the gate, that whole thing would need to be replaced. \par
\par
Ms. Candida Affa stated And did you know how much that would be? \par
\par
Ms. Mandy Tolino stated I think it's more than $5,000. And then we'd have to get a new system, and every person that has access would have to get a new card or etc, etc. Like so. And there's also you'd have to replace something on the gate to make it communicate with whatever that new system is. So it's not as straightforward as just doing a repair, which we've done in the past. It's a little it's more involved than that. \par
\par
Ms. Candida Affa stated I'm concerned. Also, if this dog isn't vaccinated or invites another dog or bites a human and could we get sued? This is our park. We don't have regulations that we're able to. \par
\par
Ms. Mandy Tolino stated so the regulations are still the expectations are still the same, that if a dog could go in there now and that could still happen. So the expectations don't change that your dog is vaccinated and licensed. The fob, someone could borrow someone's fob, they could follow someone in or a dog that's, you know, many things could happen either way. So I think there is an underlying level of risk when you take your dog to an unleashed dog area, but most of them are managed just at the owner's expense.\par
\par
Ms. Candida Affa sated we have no incidents though, so we're.  \par
\par
Ms. Mandy Tolino stated yeah, we haven't had any incidents, knock on wood. I hate to say that out loud because there, there is always a risk that something could happen, but we haven't seen anything happen. \par
\par
Ms. Candida Affa stated okay. Thanks. \par
\par
Ms. Mandy Tolino stated yeah. You're welcome. \par
\par
Ms. Natalie Santos stated any other comments from my colleagues on this Bill 83? Do we take public comment on this one? Yeah. No. \par
\par
Ms. Genesis Ortega stated yes. \par
\par
Ms. Natalie Santos stated okay. Any comments from the public on Bill 83? Alright, seeing none.\par
\par
Mr. Cristian Pungo stated I'll make a Motion to forward to the Council meeting. \par
\par
Ms. Natalie Santos stated thank you. \par
\par
\pard Ms. Natalie Santos stated and I will second that. All those in favor say I.\par
\par
\par
Mr. Cristian Pungo stated I. \cf1\kerning0\f1\par
}

Mr. Frank Kane stated so this is this is the Parks and Rec budget. I'd like to comment. You know, we've had a couple days between, between this department and between the rest of the administration. We may have gone a little overboard in the cutting of this department. I see a lot of supporters of our Parks System here behind me. I'm sure they have something to say about that. You know, as we look to make some cuts. We may have been overzealous. So I want to tell you that from the administration's perspective, we're going to we're going to maybe ask for your help in trying to, you know, look at where we can plug back in some of the money that I that I think we probably need. We had some changes after the budget submittal. You know, some of our circumstances changed. So Mandy's going to go through that with you. But I just want you to know from the administrative perspective, I don't know if there's a process for an administrative for an administration originated amendment in your in the amendments, the way that the way the Budget works here. If there is, we may put forth an Amendment or perhaps we can work with one of you to try to, to, to, to find a way to restore some of the some of the money that the Parks Department needs, whatever the process is, we're amenable to it. \par
\par
Mr. Michael Hanlon stated generally, the process is you would just submit a Budget Memo with your proposed amendment, and then council would adopt that at the Budget Amendment meeting. \par
\par
Mr. Frank Kane stated okay. Well, Mandy's going to go through the pain points with you, and you have my apology that we didn't we didn't recognize this before we submitted. \par
\par
Ms. Mandy Tolino stated thank you. I did have a presentation, if that is available. Thank you. So before I and it is a lot of information, I'm not going to dive into everything into detail, but, first, I want to thank the Parks and Rec team that's here supporting. We have the leads from each of our Bureaus. We have someone from Parks Maintenance:  Christian Bianco is here, Priscilla Reyes from Special Events; Deputy Director Lucinda Wright; Ops Manager, Rob Rhoads; Josh from the Golf; Josh Moyer from the Golf Course; Chris Hendricks, who leads Recreation, and Veronika Vostinak, who is our Capital Project Manager and oversees and oversees Sustainability Programs in, in Parks and Rec. Did I miss anybody so okay, so I just wanted to point them all out and thank them for being here tonight. So the mission of Parks and Rec is to enhance the quality of life in our city by providing and maintaining quality parks, trails and green spaces, and offering enriching recreational activities and facilities for people of all ages and abilities. The way that, that ties into the mayoral priorities in the budget are Public Safety, which includes Pedestrian Safety. So three photos below show each of those where parks plays a role in that job readiness. Through our summer seasonal hiring, where we're training young people that live in the city of Allentown who may want to become teachers or work for municipal government, around 200 or so of them each year that we onboard each summer, and then Civic Engagement. I think that we are one of the most forward facing departments.  I may be biased, but I think we're one of the most forward facing departments in the city, where we provide a lot of opportunities for residents to have civic engagement with the city. The department priorities are to invest equitably in parks and trails throughout the city, provide diverse recreation and event opportunities, create a safe and healthy work environment for the staff, increase staffing capacity to meet national standards, and preserve existing park land from development pressure. You know the next slide please. So some of the limitations that we are already dealing with is compared to national standards. The city is operating at about 60% of capacity when it comes to staffing. So compared to our size for population, there's about 40% more staff typically to take care of the amount of acres of parks that we have. So we're already starting at a point where we're in a spot where we don't have a lot of extra people to spare or extra resources to spare. As well as budgeting the 7.3 million operating the national standard for a city our size is 14, so that's not very that's a pretty wide margin. So I just want to point that out. Next slide please. And then just getting back to what frank was saying earlier, when we look at our overall budget, the picture really is when you look at the non-personnel. So when you take personnel out of the equation and look at the, the line items that are what we use to do the work that we do every day in Parks, and we're going from 1.7 to 1.4. And that's about $250,000, which doesn't seem as you know, that seems maybe to some people seems really high, some people doesn't seem quite as high, but that will for a smaller budget, that really affects the ability for us to do the work that we're doing in Parks. Next slide please. So for the General Fund, the no new positions were added to the budget. The existing budget has a decrease of around 250,000. And all of these decreases were made in our non- personnel budget. So we're asking for consideration to add back some of those funds to allow us to continue to deliver the services that we are currently providing. And the number I put on there is 172,000. And that's detailed later in the program in the presentation as well. So I'm not going to go through this whole list, but I just wanted it to be available because we've been having a really busy year, a lot of projects moving forward, many projects, successes. These are capital projects. Some of them are larger, like Bogert's bridge, some are more a little bit more community facing some resurfacing. We have pavilions, we've built Ithaca park, we've done a pavilion and resurfacing, built a mini pitch at Jordan. So that's a list of all the things that we've completed or nearing completion in 2026, including Bogert's bridge, which is almost complete. Some other successes we've seen are accepting mobile pay at our pools, which serves our young, the young people that are going to the pools and want to pay with their phone. We have Arbiter that we're using to do scheduling for our, our recreation, our Rec leagues and we are nearing event permitting in the city system, which we're hoping to launch in January. Also, just some other fun things. We were. The rose garden was named the best park in Lehigh valley sustainability hero award from. For lee valley nonprofit from the Lehigh Valley nonprofit community. The allentown golf course was voted people's choice winner of 2026, and we also were awarded a fairly large grant from the Bezos earth fund for Franklin Park. These are just some photos of the things we've done this year. You see the, the new signage and some repairs that were done to the rose garden. The top right is the mini pitch at Jordan park, Bogert's bridge in the middle, and then new art that was placed downtown and our team led the Contract that repaired that and helped get, get it downtown. Next please photo of Franklin park. Also some facelift to La Placita, which is the top right. Some of the pavilions and murals and things that we've been focused on, as well as some of our larger trail projects. Next, please. And these are our courts, so you'll probably notice them throughout the city. It's been a long time that we've really paid attention to these, but every time I drive by, I see someone using them. So it's really increased the value to people that want to play, play in our parks. Next, please. Some of the grant successes for 2026, we've received an additional $7 million in outside funding to do mostly capital projects. There is the unusual but highly valuable partnership support that supports some of our operating programs, including our Monday fun day, where we were able to have more healthy food options for people that participate, more interesting activities, as well as a an improvement to Ithaca park, which they helped fund the pavilion there. We also had a partnership with EPSA Youth Soccer that was allowed us to serve a lot of children that were learning how to play soccer. So these are kids that are not on a competitive team. They just want to try it out. So that was something new that we did this year, and we were able to do that through some partnerships. Some of the other ones listed there are a grant, an MTF grant and an LSA for the fish hatchery to do renovations at the Fish Hatchery, as well as the $4 million Bezos Earth Fund Grant, which was awarded to the allentown partnership that will be used to construct Franklin Park. Recreation success, the Recreation Bureau operated 16 programs, recording a total of 13,493 program visits. And I'll just highlight the things that were new. I sort of mentioned quickly the soccer program, and that was in partnership with pal, and that was a huge success. Every, every kid that was there was having the best time. It really was a really fun event, and we're looking forward to continuing that in the future. We also introduced a Youth Golf Program at the allentown municipal golf course, and we're hoping to grow that as we move forward with as we move forward in partnership with some of the high schools and the safety around water through the summer playground program was also a new ad, and that was able to serve a lot of children and provide them skills to be safe around, around water. These are just some pictures of some fun things that we get to do on a seasonal basis. You have the soccer program, our summer playground program, basketball, the Monday Funday, and the bottom right with the additional food opportunities, the middle one is a fireside chat, and it's just a community conversation where we show up in parks and just have conversations with people that use the parks and see what they think, and try to take that back to the office and figure out ways that we can try to implement those things in the parks. From what we're hearing from community. For aquatics, we served as this is a safety around water. Again, 170 plus kids each week over 11 sessions. So that's a lot of water safety, which is amazing. And that was the kids that sign up for the summer playground. So it was a great a great fit. We provide free pools on excessive heat days, adult lap swim, water safety, lifeguard training, and just general daily operation. Of the three pools and concession stands. Next, please for special events, we processed 97 permits so we not only deal with events that are on in parks, we deal with events that are anywhere in city owned property or city right of way. So there are 97 of those. And we are the, the collector of information through all the departments in the city. And we collected over 20,000 invoices, over 20,000 event permit fees. And this doesn't include fees that are, are billed via other departments. That's just strictly per event permit fees. We ran successfully ran city run events which are listed there. And these are ones that we run from start to finish. We staff them, we plan them, we manage everything. For these events that are listed there. And then we also manage contracted and partnered concerts. And that is the union terrace concerts with Arts Quest as well as BOMBA at the beach with PRCP and finally, we manage the chamber of commerce contract, which helps us to additional events including Fiesta, Blues, Liberty Bell Tree Lighting and New Year's Eve.  This just is a detail of the reach, so a lot of these events range in attendance from 2,000 all the way up to 20,000. So a lot of people are attending events in Allentown. Despite a national trend of people not going to large events. Like we're still seeing a good turnout to our events and we don't always define the success of an event by the number of people that attend, but the events that are larger, we get good attendance and some of the smaller community events. We get really great engagement for the people that do attend. Just some photos. This Lights in the Parkway are Walking Monday around a campfire egg hunt. We have BOMBA at the beach. Photos the union terrace concerts, as well as the Halloweekend, which I know some of you had gone this weekend. It was a great event, a lot of fun. A lot of kids came out. It was a wonderful time. And these photos are from the morning call. Who was there to, to document it? But it was a really great, great weekend.  For park maintenance, we maintain 2,000 plus acres of Parkland and 35 Parks, and this is with 53 full time staff members. The primary focus of the maintenance team is landscape and playground maintenance, trash and recycling. We do a lot of response to vandalism and illegal dumping restrooms. We manage the, the, the maintenance side of the pools. Also, we support events and recreation for the band trailer, movie screen, downtown decorations, lights in the parkway. Capital Project Construction, Arboriculture, Managing trees, citywide snow removal, plantings and plantings and medians and along Hamilton. So that's just some photos for the maintenance. We have our sustainability success. As I mentioned, Lehigh Valley sustainability hero award. We also are working through Urban Forest Master Plan and plantings throughout the city, and that's in the public right of way youth climate action. We're entering year three, and that has been a great program where each year it's a connection with youth in the city, giving them a chance to share their ideas on how to come up with projects that are related to sustainability. Currently underway is the Climate Action Plan. There's a lot of public meetings and public input and engagement that's happening right now, as well as EV Fleet Pilot, and I didn't put it on the slide, but we had received money for a citizen science project for air quality with Community Bike Works. That was a $16,000 grant award, as well as $50,000 technical assistance grant for energy management in our city buildings so and then those are some photos of the youth climate action. And then this is getting into the details of the pain points. So the highest dollar cuts in our 2027 Budget, compared to 26 are in the Special Events, Other Contract Services. And that is a decrease of about 100,000, which is approximately 27% of that line. The next is Contract Services and Grounds Maintenance, $50,000 decrease, which is about 24% and then we have our Lights in the Parkway, which is a 23% in the over the overall total program. And many of these are in maintenance and supplies and if you consider inflation, it's more painful than just what's being decreased in those lines. Next, please. So in summary, the ground level operational capacity shrinks even though if you look at our overall budget amount rises slightly due to increases in personnel. So you can't we cannot we don't have the same buying capacity for supplies, equipment, materials or training. So our ability to keep staff certified and do the work we need to do is, is decreased. The next slide. So this is the, the overview for, for Maintenance. So these are all the lines that are below personnel. So if you look at that, that shows the 2026 comparison to the 2027 proposed and the lines that were decreased and the change is at $73,564 proposed decrease. So I'm suggesting that we add about $27,000 back into that in order to allow us to continue operating at the level that we're operating or close to it. Next slide please, for Special Events. Again, this is one of the hardest hits, the $100,000 cut to special events impacts, ability to deliver programs that drive community participation and cultural vibrancy. So a lot of this is programs, partnerships, and some of our contracted events through the Chamber or looking at decreasing 4th of July or Juneteenth events, reevaluating and maybe shrinking some of the those, those type of events and again, this is just the one line, the 46 Other Contract Services that was the $100,000 decrease. Lights in the Parkway, so this is a revenue neutral account based on sponsorships, both in-kind monetary as well as ticket sales. So the total reductions were 24%. Most of that was in marketing, which we think we can primarily make up in sponsorships, we're hopeful. But the other part was in materials and supplies. So that means that we're not going to be able to purchase a new light display for, for this year. Please, so that is the lights in the Parkway Budget Summary.  Sustainability has a very small budget. It's mostly just personnel. It's about a $10,000 Budget. So I think that once the Climate Action Plan is complete, it would be great to consider adding additional funding for implementation projects in the sustainability budget in future years. Not, not asking for that for 27, but maybe 2028. Once the Climate Action Plan is complete. Next, please. Recreation. Recreation is. Recreation. Budget is in a decent position, and they have the tools that they need primarily to provide the same Rec opportunities in 2027 as 2026, which is a good thing. And we will, at the end of the year, always look back and see which events we think are what which Recreation Programs went really well, and if there are changes that need to be made, but no major issues with Recreation. Aquatics, training was cut. So this will affect our ability to cover Lifeguard Certification for youth that work for us and our lifeguards in Allentown. So we offer that free for Allentown residents only. If you're not allentown resident, you would have to pay for your certification. But this budget line was to support the people to get their lifeguard certs in Allentown. And also Operating Materials were reduced. And part of that is for our. We use Operating Materials and Supplies to buy supplies that we resell in our concession stands. So that is something that is also a way to increase revenue is the more we spend on supplies, then we resell them, resell them, and, you know, make a profit in the concession stands. So that was the general fund. The Trexler fund is its own separate fund          and in 27 we had proposed adding one position to the Trexler fund, funded through the Trexler fund. And in order to do this, that, that increase in personnel costs required a decrease to some of our operational capacity. Just pointing that out as, as a note, not, not necessarily, you know, a major issue or change, but just that in order to add a position, we reduced our. Our line 54 and, and 68. Next, please. And then the goal fund, the goal fund is doing really well. They anticipate that the revenues will increase next year. There is a projected fee increase. And each year we put aside funding from that's from the Golf Course Revenue into a capital account, and that is used for irrigation, not aeration. That's a typo. It's an irrigation project, which is in the works right now for design. And then we're going to hopefully move into move towards construction in the coming years for irrigation repairs at the golf course, you can look forward to a new Golf Simulator that's happening this year. And also there is an upgrade to the Assistant Greenskeeper and Equipment Tech that will be hitting the golf course fund, likely in 20, either in December of this year or in 2027 and that's been put through previously. Our Capital Budget that lists the Projects that are both grant and outside funded, as well as the 2027 anticipated needs for the City Bond, and that would be for Parks Operation Facility, which supports the safety of our employees. We want to make sure that we have a safe place for all the employees to work out of. And right now, currently, that's we don't have that Mack Pool design, MLK Trail, Fountain Park Design, as well as safety surfacing. So you may have noticed that Cedar Beach Playground is closed. We are removing the safety surfacing and replacing that. So we're going to do the same thing up at Bucky Boyle as well. So and I think that's it. That was a lot. Sorry. \par

And i think it is critically important that we try to restore that funding in any way we can, whether through, you know, private funding or grants, because having our urban youth, being able to take on being lifeguards serve, you know, one job training extremely important to, to be role models to the youth of allentown, to get kids to learn how to swim, to see what it can lead to in terms of, you know, teenage employment, etc. I think is just critically important. So like i said, it struck a nerve. I would and i'll be happy to work with mandy to look at other funding opportunities. But i think it's really critically important. Thank you. Rodney bush. All right. Thank you guys for having me today. \par
          [01:20:11]\par
My name is rodney bush. I am a vested member of the city of allentown. And there's a lyric that holds dear to my heart. It is she yells, selling's a sin. But so is telling young men that selling's a sin if you don't offer new ways to win. Now, we're seeing across the country that cities that invest in community, that invest in community, events, that invest in community services, that they're having drastic drops in crime and violence. Cities like chicago and baltimore and detroit and new york. In fact, when you invest in parks and recs and city events, there is a 18% decrease in serious crimes, as per the american study done by the american for arts, there's also a 14% fewer reported reports of child abuse, and there's also an increase in community unity. What community events do it does a major job in building safety and community for our citizens of allentown. The broad consumer tracking shows that 89% of americans believe that local events are vital to the health and the well-being of the community as a whole. 89% of americans believe that. We've seen that when there are civic engagement opportunities and community events, that people are 50% more likely to volunteer. And there was a mention about the return on investment. When we invest in community engagement and community events in parks and rec, right? For every dollar spent, you're getting a return of $144, $1.2 million invested generates $177 million total in savings by reducing local shootings and homicides for every dollar invested in public health and public community and these community events, you're getting return of $41 for every single dollar invested in our communities. We are saving $41 in combined medical, community health, mental health and crime and legal expenses. So i urge city council to revisit the communities budget because again, budgets are value statements, right? Where i put my money and my household tells and dictates the life of my wife, the life of my family, and in turn impacts the community as a whole. So again, i urge the city council members and the mayor to relook at the cuts that they are making in our community, as they have drastic impacts on our youth. Thank you. That was it. Okay. \par
          thank you. I believe we still have bill 82 and bill 85. Or was that? Okay? Gotcha, gotcha, gotcha, gotcha. All right. Is there anything else for parks and rec that you would like to share? I just wanted to say i'm really blown away by the amount of people that showed up tonight. I'm super grateful. I know it's difficult to come out on an evening, so i just want to say thank you so much. And i love the statement of the budgets or value statement. And i think that's was really great to hear the value that parks brings to the table. So regardless of line by line budgeting, parks are valuable. And i'm grateful to be able to have this conversation and answer the questions. And i'm happy to follow up with any questions after this meeting as well to kind of just explain and but i do think the community explained it the best of the value that parks brings to the city of allentown. So i just wanted to say thank you so much for everyone who came out. And i'm really blown away and impressed and grateful for your time. Thank you. And we look forward to seeing that budget memo coming up. So with that, i'll adjourn this meeting\par
